IUT2.Rem2_5_1.content: (i) Relative to the standard cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism of Proposition 1.3 (ii) and the resulting Kummer map (delta of Corollary 2.5 (ii) taken to be the identity), for j in |F_l| the set theta^j(Pi_v) consists of precisely the mu_{2l}-orbit of the theta value qq_v^{j^2}, where j is the element of {0, 1, ..., l*} determined by j. (ii) The reciprocals of the l-th powers of these theta values (not the theta values themselves) correspond to the values Theta-ddot(+-sqrt(-1) . q_X^{j/2}) of the theta series Theta-ddot of [EtTh] Proposition 1.4, i.e. to values at points separated by periods from +-sqrt(-1); they have the property that Theta-ddot(c)/Theta-ddot(c') is a root of unity for c' obtained from c by an automorphism of Pi_v with c'/c a unit. (iii) The mu_{2l}-multiple indeterminacies for different j in |F_l| are independent, not synchronized; each arises from the action of (Delta^+-_v / Delta_v)^delta, of order 2l.
IUT2.Rem2_5_1.conclusion: theta^j(Pi_v) = mu_{2l} . qq_v^{j^2} (as orbits) for j = 0, ..., l*; the reciprocals of the l-th powers of these values correspond to Theta-ddot(+-sqrt(-1) . q_X^{j/2}); the mu_{2l}-indeterminacies for distinct j are independent.
obligations: The label bookkeeping is formalized as a fragment, and the classical identities behind part (ii) are formalized as fragments for the theta series of [EtTh] Proposition 1.4 over a complete normed field, with q_X = r^2: the functional equations, the values at +-sqrt(-1) q_X^{j/2}, and the mu_{2l}-orbit form of the relation with qq^{j^2}. IUT2.Rem2_6_3.content: For a subgraph Gamma' of the line graph Gamma_Y (vertices Z), single-basepoint and splitting considerations force Gamma' connected and containing 0. For finite Gamma' define ||Gamma'|| = |Gamma'|^{-1} . sum over j in F_l* of min over integers j in (fiber of j) intersect Gamma' of j^2, where |Gamma'| is the cardinality of the image in F_l* of the nonzero vertices and the min over the empty set is 0. Claim (d): as a function of |Gamma'| this is a monotone increasing but not strictly increasing positive rational function that attains its maximum at |Gamma'| = l* and is constant for |Gamma'| >= l*.

IUT2.Rem2_6_3.conclusion: Maximizing ||Gamma'|| is achieved by Gamma'_Y-black-triangle (vertices 0, ..., l*), and the values qq_v^{j^2} are thereby distinguished.
obligations: Kernel-checked only for the elementary arithmetic: for Gamma' with vertex set [-a, b], |Gamma'| = min(max(a,b), l*) and ||Gamma'|| = (n+1)(2n+1)/6 with n = |Gamma'|, which is strictly increasing in n; hence ||Gamma'|| is monotone in max(a,b), maximal exactly when max(a,b) >= l*, with maximum l(l+1)/12. Infinite Gamma' (part (iii)) is not treated.
ambiguities: Page 79 defines |Gamma'| as the size of a subset of F_l*, so |Gamma'| <= l* always. IUT2.Rem3_6_4.content: Explains why objects are known only up to isomorphism: Kummer N-th power morphisms respect multiplication but not addition, hence act as Frobenius-type morphisms between distinct ring structures, forcing the rigidity theory of [EtTh]. Galois evaluation is linear, so the first power of the theta function (and of its values) is the only power that crosses the mono-theta bridge; N-th powers for N > 1 are only defined as (-)^N of the first power, and other powers are not horizontal for the multiradial connection structure.

IUT2.Cor3_7.content: Group-theoretic Gaussian monoids and uniradiality, in the situation of Proposition 3.4: the full poly-isomorphism M^Theta_*(Pi_v) -> M^Theta_*(dagger F_v) of projective systems of mono-theta environments, M^Theta_*(Pi_v) from Proposition 1.2 (i) and dagger F_v a tempered Frobenioid as in Proposition 3.3. For M^Theta_*(Pi_v), Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot}(M^Theta_{* black-triangle-double-dot}) and G_v(...) are identified with Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot} and G_v(Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot}); subscripts |t| and <F_l^*> as in Corollaries 3.5, 3.6. (i) From group-theoretic to post-anabelian Gaussian monoids: each isomorphism M^Theta_*(Pi_v) -> M^Theta_*(dagger F_v) induces compatible isomorphisms infinity-Psi^iota_env(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)) -> infinity-Psi_xi(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)) -> infinity-Psi_xi(M^Theta_*(dagger F_v)) -> infinity-Psi_{F_xi}(dagger F_v) and the same without infinity, with the actions of Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot} and the labeled G_v copies, and on units Psi^iota_env(...)^x -> Psi_xi(...)^x -> Psi_{F_xi}(dagger F_v)^x with G_v(Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot})_{<F_l^*>}; the left portion is Corollary 3.5 (ii) for M^Theta_*(Pi_v), the right portion Corollary 3.6 (ii), joined by functoriality. (ii) Uniradiality of Gaussian monoids: with Psi_{F_xi}(dagger F_v)^{x mu} the quotient of the units by torsion, the functorial algorithms Pi_v -> Psi_gau(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)), infinity-Psi_gau(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)) (with splittings up to torsion and the G_v-action), composed from Proposition 1.2 (i) and Corollary 3.5 (ii), (iii), depend on the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism of Corollary 1.11 (b) (through the surjection of Remark 1.11.5 (i) used in Proposition 3.1 (ii) and Corollary 3.5 (ii)), hence fail to be compatible with automorphisms of the pair G_v(M^Theta_*(dagger F_v))_{<F_l^*>} acting on Psi_{F_xi}(dagger F_v)^{x mu} that arise from automorphisms of the pair with Psi_{F_xi}(dagger F_v)^x; as given, the algorithm only admits a uniradial formulation.

an isomorphism M^Theta_*(Pi_v) -> M^Theta_*(dagger F_v) of projective systems of mono-theta environments
IUT2.Cor3_7.conclusion: (i) compatible isomorphisms from group-theoretic Gaussian monoids to Frobenioid-theoretic (post-anabelian) Gaussian monoids and on their units; (ii) the group-theoretic Gaussian monoid algorithms are not compatible with automorphisms of the unit pair modulo torsion, so they only admit a uniradial formulation.

IUT2.Def3_8.content: Frobenioid interpretations of the monoids of Section 3. (i) The monoids with Pi_X(M^Theta_*)-action, Psi_cns(M^Theta_*) and Psi_{dagger C_v} (Propositions 3.1 (ii), 3.3 (ii)), give p_v-adic Frobenioids F_cns(M^Theta_*), F_{dagger C_v} of monoid type Z ([FrdII] Example 1.1 (ii)) whose divisor monoid at each object of B^temp(Pi_X(M^Theta_*))^0 is isomorphic to Q>=0; there is a tautological isomorphism dagger C_v -> F_{dagger C_v}, used to identify them, so Proposition 3.3 (ii) becomes an isomorphism dagger C_v -> F_cns(M^Theta_*), with a mono-analytic version dagger C^{|-}_v -> F^{|-}_cns(M^Theta_*), a labeled version (dagger C^{|-}_v)_{|t|} -> (F^{|-}_cns(M^Theta_*))_{|t|}, and Frobenioid-theoretic versions of the constructions of Corollaries 3.5 (iii), 3.6 (iii) such as (F^{|-}_cns)_0 -> (F^{|-}_cns)_{<F_l^*>}. (ii) The monoids with topological group action G_v acting on Psi^iota_env, Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v, alpha}, Psi_xi, Psi_{F_xi}(dagger F_v) give p_v-adic Frobenioids F^iota_env(M^Theta_*), F_{dagger F^Theta_v, alpha}, F_xi(M^Theta_*), F_{F_xi}(dagger F_v) of monoid type Z with divisor monoid N and splittings; F_env := {F^iota_env}_iota, F_{dagger F^Theta_v} := {F_{dagger F^Theta_v, alpha}}_alpha, F_gau := {F_xi}_xi, F_{F_gau}(dagger F_v) := {F_{F_xi}}_xi. A tautological isomorphism dagger C^Theta_v -> F_{dagger F^Theta_v, alpha}, compatible with splittings, identifies them, so the third display of Corollary 3.6 (ii) gives isomorphisms of split Frobenioids F_{dagger F^Theta_v, alpha} -> F^iota_env -> F_xi -> F_{F_xi}(dagger F_v), compatible with the subcategories F_{2l . xi} determined by Psi_{2l . xi}, hence F_{dagger F^Theta_v} -> F_env -> F_gau -> F_{F_gau}(dagger F_v). (iii) The direct products defining Psi_xi and Psi_{F_xi} give natural embeddings of categories F_xi(M^Theta_*) -> product over |t| in F_l^* of F^{|-}_cns(M^Theta_*)_{|t|} =: F^{|-}_cns(M^Theta_*)_{F_l^*} and F_{F_xi}(dagger F_v) -> (dagger C^{|-}_v)_{F_l^*}, coinciding on F_{2l . xi}; as xi varies these are the Gaussian distributions (Fig. 3.3). There are also diagonal embeddings F^{|-}_cns -> F^{|-}_cns_{<F_l^*>} -> F^{|-}_cns_{F_l^*} and the same for dagger C^{|-}_v, the constant distributions.
explicit_hypotheses: The setting of Section 3 (Propositions 3.1, 3.3, Corollaries 3.5, 3.6)
IUT2.Def3_8.conclusion: Definition (no proof obligation): Frobenioids F_cns, F_env, F_xi, F_gau, F_{F_gau} with tautological identifications, isomorphisms F_{dagger F^Theta_v} -> F_env -> F_gau -> F_{F_gau}(dagger F_v), and the Gaussian and constant distributions as embeddings of categories.

IUT2.Prop4_4.content: Frobenioid-theoretic Gaussian monoids at archimedean v. With the notation of Proposition 4.3, dagger F_v = (dagger C_v, dagger D_v, dagger kappa_v) the data at v in V^arc of a Theta-Hodge theater dagger HT^Theta, dagger F^vdash_v = (dagger C^vdash_v, dagger D^vdash_v, dagger tau^vdash_v) the data at v of the associated F^vdash-prime-strip, dagger U_v := dagger D_v and dagger U^{+-}_v, dagger U^cor_v the corresponding Aut-holomorphic orbispaces. (i) (Constant monoids) The Kummer structure dagger kappa_v: Psi_{dagger F_v} := O^triangleright(dagger C_v) -> A_{dagger D_v} and the tautological equality dagger D_v = dagger U_v determine a unique isomorphism of topological monoids Psi_{dagger F_v} -> Psi_cns(dagger U_v). (ii) (Mono-analytic semi-simplifications) With Psi_{dagger F^vdash_v} := O^triangleright(dagger C^vdash_v), there is a unique {+-1}-orbit of isomorphisms of topological groups Psi^x_{dagger F^vdash_v} -> Psi_cns(dagger D^vdash_v)^x and a unique isomorphism of monoids Psi^R_{dagger F^vdash_v} := Psi_{dagger F^vdash_v}/Psi^x_{dagger F^vdash_v} -> Psi^R_cns(dagger D^vdash_v) = R_{>=0}(dagger D^vdash_v) sending the distinguished element determined by p_v = e = 2.71828... (the element whose natural logarithm is 1) to log^{dagger D^vdash_v}(p_v); with Psi^ss_{dagger F^vdash_v} := Psi^x x Psi^R, these give a natural poly-isomorphism Psi^ss_{dagger F^vdash_v} -> Psi^ss_cns(dagger D^vdash_v) compatible with the splittings, and Psi^ss_{dagger F_v} := Psi^ss_{dagger F^vdash_v} gives a natural isomorphism Psi^ss_{dagger F_v} -> Psi^ss_{dagger F^vdash_v}. (iii) (Labels, F_l^{x+-}-symmetries, conjugate synchronization) The isomorphism of (i) determines, for each t in LabCusp^{+-}(dagger U_v), compatible isomorphisms (Psi_{dagger F_v})_t -> Psi_cns(dagger U_v)_t and F_l^{x+-}-symmetrizing isomorphisms (from F_l^{x+-} = Gal(dagger U^{+-}_v/dagger U^cor_v) acting on the Gal(dagger U_v/dagger U^{+-}_v)-orbits of cusps) between data indexed by distinct t, determining diagonal submonoids and an isomorphism (Psi_{dagger F_v})_0 -> (Psi_{dagger F_v})_{<F_l^*>}. (iv) (Theta and Gaussian monoids) The monoids Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v}, Psi_{F_gau}(dagger F_v) with natural splittings, determined via (i) to (iii) by Psi_env(dagger U_v), Psi_gau(dagger U_v) of Proposition 4.3 (iv), come with natural isomorphisms Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v} -> Psi_env(dagger U_v) -> Psi_gau(dagger U_v) -> Psi_{F_gau}(dagger F_v) that restrict to the identity or to (the restriction to units of) the isomorphism of (i) or its inverse on the copies of Psi^x_{dagger F_v}, Psi_cns(dagger U_v)^x, and are compatible with the natural splittings.

IUT2.Rem4_7_3.content: F_l^{x+-} versus F_l*-symmetry: F_l approximates Z; F_l^{x+-} corresponds to addition, involves the zero label and units, and is applied for conjugate synchronization (uniradial, but coric after mono-analyticization); F_l* corresponds to multiplication, separates the zero label, describes the Gaussian monoids as functions of j in F_l*, and is multiradial. Volumes at each j in F_l* are given weight 1/l* so that the diagonal constant distribution has weight 1.
IUT2.Rem4_7_3.conclusion: F_l^{x+-}-symmetry (additive, with the zero label, used for conjugate synchronization) and F_l*-symmetry (multiplicative, separating the zero label, used for the Gaussian monoids as functions of j) play different roles; the volume at each j in F_l* gets weight 1/l*, so the diagonal constant distribution has total weight 1.
obligations: The weighted average (1/l*) . sum j^2 is computed in a fragment; the paper does not state its value.

IUT2.Cor4_8.content: Frobenioid-theoretic monoids associated to Theta NF-Hodge theaters. Let dagger HT^{Theta NF} = (dagger F^{circledast} <-- dagger F^{circledcirc} <- dagger F_J -> dagger F_> --> dagger HT^Theta) be a Theta NF-Hodge theater ([IUTchI] Definition 5.5 (iii)) lifting the D-Theta NF-Hodge theater of Corollary 4.7 and glued to the Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theater of Corollary 4.6 via [IUTchI] Proposition 6.7 (J = T^*). (i) Non-realified global structures: a functorial algorithm in dagger F^{circledcirc} (or dagger F^{circledast}), using isomorphisms of cyclotomes and Kummer maps ([IUTchI] Example 5.1 (v), (vi)), constructs Kummer isomorphisms of pseudo-monoids {pi_1^{kappa-sol} acting on dagger M^{circledast}_{infinity kappa}} -> {pi_1^{kappa-sol}(dagger D^{circledast}) acting on M^{circledast}_{infinity kappa}(dagger D^{circledcirc})} and dagger M^{circledast}_kappa -> M^{circledast}_kappa(dagger D^{circledcirc}) (the first two with group actions, up to a single conjugacy indeterminacy), and by restricting Kummer classes the Kummer-theoretic isomorphisms for M^{circledast}, M-bar^{circledast}, M^{circledast}_sol, M^{circledast}_mod, M-bar^{circledast}_mod, read as compatible isomorphisms of Frobenioids dagger F^{circledcirc} -> F^{circledcirc}(dagger D^{circledcirc}), dagger F^{circledast} -> F^{circledast}(dagger D^{circledcirc}), dagger F^{circledast}_mod -> F^{circledast}_mod(dagger D^{circledcirc}) and the realified one. (ii) Labels and F_l^*-symmetry: in the notation of Corollary 4.7 (ii), Corollary 4.6 (i) applied to the F-prime-strips of the capsule dagger F_J and the isomorphisms of (i) give, for each j in LabCusp(dagger D^{circledcirc}) (-> J), isomorphisms dagger F_j -> dagger F^{circledcirc}|_j -> F^{circledcirc}(dagger D^{circledcirc})|_j and labeled Kummer isomorphisms of the global monoids and Frobenioids, with F_l^*-symmetrizing isomorphisms from the poly-action of F_l^* on dagger F^{circledcirc} ([IUTchI] Example 4.3 (iv), Corollary 5.3 (i)); objects with pi_1^rat-actions have independent pi_1^{rat / kappa-sol}-conjugacy indeterminacies for distinct j and a single j-independent pi_1^{kappa-sol}-conjugacy indeterminacy; compatible via dagger zeta_* with the F_l^*-symmetry of the NF-bridge ([IUTchI] Proposition 4.9 (i), Corollary 5.6 (ii)), determining diagonal objects in the formal sense of Corollary 4.7 (ii). (iii) Localization functors and realified global structures: for j in LabCusp(dagger D^{circledcirc}) (labels v_j for v in V_mod), a functorial algorithm in the NF-bridge constructs mutually compatible localization functors and poly-morphisms (dagger F^{circledast}_mod)_j -> dagger F_j, (dagger F^{circledast R}_mod)_j -> dagger F^R_j, {pi_1^{kappa-sol} acting on dagger M^{circledast}_{infinity kappa}}_j -> dagger M_{infinity kappa v_j} within dagger M_{infinity kappa x v_j}, compatible with the Kummer isomorphisms of (i), (ii) and with Corollary 4.7 (iii), and a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids dagger C^{||-}_j -> (dagger F^{circledast R}_mod)_j compatible with the Prime bijections and the local isomorphisms (Remark 4.8.3) and with the F_l^*-symmetrizing isomorphisms.

glued to the Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theater of Corollary 4.6 via [IUTchI] Proposition 6.7, J = T^*
IUT2.Cor4_8.conclusion: (i) Kummer isomorphisms of global pseudo-monoids and Frobenioids; (ii) labeled isomorphisms and F_l^*-symmetrizing isomorphisms with the conjugacy pattern of Corollary 4.7 (ii); (iii) localization functors and a natural isomorphism dagger C^{||-}_j -> (dagger F^{circledast R}_mod)_j, all compatible.

IUT2.Def4_9.content: Kummer structures and prime-strips. (i) For a Frobenioid C whose base category D is isomorphic to the connected finite etale coverings of the spectrum of an MLF or a CAF, and a universal covering pro-object A of D with G := Aut(A), evaluating O^{triangleright}(-) ([FrdI] Proposition 2.2) at A gives G acting on O^{triangleright}(A), with mu_N(A) within O^mu(A) within O^x(A) and quotients O^x(A) -> O^{x mu_N}(A) -> O^{x mu}(A). For G nontrivial (the MLF case), a x-Kummer structure (respectively x mu-Kummer structure) on C is a Zhat^x-orbit (respectively Ism-orbit) of isomorphisms of ind-topological G-modules kappa^x: O^x(G) -> O^x(A) (respectively kappa^{x mu}: O^{x mu}(G) -> O^{x mu}(A)), independent of the choice of A; any x-Kummer structure is unique (Remark 1.11.1 (b)); a x mu-Kummer structure determines and is determined by the submodules I^kappa_H(A) := Im(O^x(G)^H) within O^{x mu}(A) for open H within G. (Split-)Kummer Frobenioids are (split) Frobenioids with such a structure. (ii) For an F^{|-}-prime-strip double-dagger F^{|-} and w in V^bad, double-dagger F^{|-}_w is split with base category double-dagger D^{|-}_w; the 2l-torsion mu_{2l} of O^x and the images of the splittings generate O^perp within O^{triangleright}, O^{black-triangle} := O^perp / mu_{2l} (so O^{triangleright}/O^x -> O^{black-triangle}), and O^{black-triangle x mu} := O^{black-triangle} x O^{x mu}; Remark 1.11.1 (b) gives a unique Zhat^x-orbit kappa^{|- x}_w: O^x(double-dagger G) -> O^x(double-dagger A), inducing an Ism-orbit kappa^{|- x mu}_w. (iii) The rational function monoid of O^{black-triangle x mu} with the divisor monoid of double-dagger F^{|-}_w gives a split model Frobenioid ([FrdI] Theorem 5.2 (ii)) with a x mu-Kummer structure, written double-dagger F^{|- black-triangle x mu}_w; double-dagger F^{|-}_w also denotes the split-Kummer Frobenioid with the x-Kummer structure. (iv) For w in V^good intersected with V^non, the same with O^{black-triangle} := O^perp (no quotient by mu_{2l}). (v) For w in V^arc, double-dagger F^{|- black-triangle x mu}_w replaces the split Frobenioid by the inductive system of its quotients by N-torsion, N in a cofinal subset of N>=1, with compatible surjections (double-dagger D^{|-}_w)^x -> O^{x mu_N}(A) defined up to the nontrivial automorphism of (double-dagger D^{|-}_w)^x, a sort of Kummer structure. (vi) double-dagger F^{|- black-triangle x mu} := {double-dagger F^{|- black-triangle x mu}_v}_{v in V} from (iii), (iv), (v); replacing split Frobenioids by those with trivial splittings (subcategories of isometries, [FrdI] Theorem 5.1 (iii), [FrdII] Example 3.3 (iii)) gives double-dagger F^{|- x} and double-dagger F^{|- x mu}, split-x- and split-x mu-Kummer Frobenioids at v in V^non. (vii) For |-box in {|-x, |-x mu, |-black-triangle x mu}, an F^{|-box}-prime-strip is a collection {*F^{|-box}_v}_{v in V} with each member isomorphic to double-dagger F^{|-box}_v; morphisms are collections of isomorphisms indexed by V. (viii) An F^{||- black-triangle x mu}-prime-strip is *F^{||- black-triangle x mu} = (*C^{||-}, Prime(*C^{||-}) -> V, *F^{|- black-triangle x mu}, {*rho_v}_{v in V}) satisfying (a) to (f) of [IUTchI] Definition 5.2 (iv) with the F^{|-}-prime-strip replaced by an F^{|- black-triangle x mu}-prime-strip; the generators of the monoids O^{black-triangle}(-) (each abstractly isomorphic to N) at v in V^bad (nonempty), with the rho_w, determine up to isomorphism an object of the global realified Frobenioid *C^{||-} of negative arithmetic degree, the pilot object; morphisms are isomorphisms of the data.
explicit_hypotheses: For (i): C a Frobenioid with base category isomorphic to the finite etale coverings of Spec of an MLF or CAF
For (ii) to (viii): double-dagger F^{|-} = {double-dagger F^{|-}_v}_{v in V} an F^{|-}-prime-strip relative to the initial Theta-data
IUT2.Def4_9.conclusion: Definition (no proof obligation): x- and x mu-Kummer structures and Kummer Frobenioids; the split-Kummer Frobenioids F^{|- black-triangle x mu}_v; F^{|-x}-, F^{|-x mu}-, F^{|- black-triangle x mu}- and F^{||- black-triangle x mu}-prime-strips with their morphisms; the pilot object.

IUT2.Ex1_8.content: Concrete multiradial environments, each defined by radial data, coric data and a radial algorithm whose radial functor is full and essentially surjective. (i) Radial data (Pi, G, alpha): Pi isomorphic to the tempered group Pi^tp of X_k (double underline), G isomorphic to G_k, alpha the full poly-isomorphism Pi/Delta -> G of topological groups; coric data a topological group isomorphic to G_k; radial algorithm (Pi, G, alpha) -> G (compare IUT I Fig. 3.2, Fig. 1.2). (ii) Using the algorithms (*_TM) Pi -> (Pi acting on M_TM(Pi)) and (*_triangleright) G -> (G acting on O^triangleright(G)) and the tautological isomorphism (*_TM triangleright), radial data (Pi on M_TM(Pi), G on O^triangleright(G), alpha_triangleright) with alpha_triangleright the induced poly-isomorphism of MLF-Galois TM-pairs; radial algorithm to (G on O^triangleright(G)). (iii) For a closed subgroup Gamma of Zhat^x, the unit versions (*_x) with M^x_TM(Pi), O^x(G) and alpha_x the Gamma-orbit of the poly-isomorphism induced by alpha_triangleright; isomorphisms of coric data are Gamma-multiples. (iv) Torsion versions (*_mu) and quotients M^{x mu} = M^x/M^mu, O^{x mu} = O^x/O^mu (*_{x mu}); cyclotomic and co-cyclotomic versions of (iii); Ism(G), the compact group of G-isometries of O^{x mu}(G); closed subgroups Gamma^{x mu} of Ism(-) preserved by isomorphisms G_1 -> G_2 may replace Gamma (examples: Ism itself, and the image of Zhat^x -> Z_p^x in Ism). (v) Radial data (Pi on M^mu_TM(Pi), G on O^{x mu}(G), alpha_{mu, x mu}), with alpha_{mu, x mu} the poly-morphism determined by the full poly-isomorphism Pi/Delta -> G and the trivial homomorphism M^mu_TM(Pi) -> O^{x mu}(G); isomorphisms are Gamma^{x mu}-multiples; radial algorithm to (G on O^{x mu}(G)). (vi) Replacing M^mu_TM(Pi) by Pi_mu(M^Theta_*(Pi)) tensor Q/Z gives an exterior-cyclotomic version of (v). (vii) Groupification algorithms (*_gp) and their profinite completions (*_gp-hat), with a Gamma-action and a poly-isomorphism alpha_gp-hat compatible with alpha_x. (viii) Radial data (Pi on M_TM(Pi), G on O^gp-hat(G), alpha_{triangleright, x mu}), a diagram of poly-morphisms through the groupifications and O^x(G) onto O^{x mu}(G); coric data as in (v) with Gamma^{x mu} = Im(Gamma); radial algorithm to (G on O^{x mu}(G)). (ix) The log-shell I(G) in O^{x mu}(G) (p^{-1} times the image of the G-invariants of O^x(G)); replacing G on O^{x mu}(G) by (G on O^{x mu}(G), I(G)) in (v), (vi), (viii) gives log-shell versions.

IUT2.Rem3_5_2.content: Significance of the symmetrizing isomorphisms of Corollary 3.5 (i). (i) Combinatorial model: for the ordered set E = {0, 1} with 0 < 1 and underlying unordered set S, Aut(S) = Z/2Z, a factorization of a construction F on ordered two-element sets through a construction F^sym(S) with Aut(S)-action is a collection of symmetrizing isomorphisms, i.e. descent data to the orbiset quotient, which never violates the bijection between E and S (though via an indeterminate bijection). The naive approach, collapsing to the coarse quotient Q = {*}, forces an Aut(S)-equivariant assignment of each s in S to all points of E_Q = {0_Q, 1_Q}, giving 4 possibilities, some not bijective; synchronizing them would need an automorphism of the order on E_Q swapping its two points, which cannot exist. This contrast of crushing E to a point versus symmetrizing without violating the bijection is the topic of [IUTchI] Remarks 4.9.2 (i), 6.12.4 (i), Fig. 4.5. (ii) Without an F_l^{x+-}-symmetry the single basepoint (Remark 2.6.1 (i)) rigidifies the labels as well as the conjugates; the symmetry eliminates this, allowing (a) symmetrizing isomorphisms, (b) a bijective link with the labels LabCusp^+-(Pi_X(M^Theta_*)), needed for Gaussian monoids with distinct values at distinct labels, (c) relative to a single basepoint, needed for conjugate synchronization. (iii) The symmetry arises from a Delta_X-outer action, conjugation by geometric rather than arithmetic elements, which is crucial for conjugate synchronization of the copies of G_v(M^Theta_*) ([IUTchI] Remark 6.12.6 (ii)). (iv) Conjugate synchronization via symmetry is a nonarchimedean counterpart of conjugate synchronization via the connectedness of Gamma^{black-triangle}_X (Remarks 2.6.1 (i), 2.8.3). (v) Section 4 extends these ideas to the global portion and to good v of a D-Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theater.
IUT2.Rem3_5_2.conclusion: Commentary: symmetrizing isomorphisms act as descent data preserving the bijection with labels, unlike collapsing labels; the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry gives (a), (b), (c) simultaneously.
obligations: Nothing to formalize.

IUT2.Rem3_6_2.content: On the diagram in the third display of Corollary 3.6 (ii), summarized as Fig. 3.1 (Frobenioid-theoretic theta monoids => group-theoretic theta monoids via Kummer, Galois evaluation down to group-theoretic Gaussian monoids, and 'forget' back to Frobenioid-theoretic Gaussian monoids). (i) The three portions correspond to Kummer, Galois evaluation and forgetting; forgetting yields post-anabelian monoids; the composite of Kummer and evaluation is a comparison isomorphism between Frobenius-like and etale-like structures, as in classical Hodge-Arakelov theory where the comparison isomorphism comes from evaluating theta functions and their derivatives at torsion points. (ii) Etale-like structures (etale or tempered fundamental groups) are invariant under non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters such as the Theta-link and the log-wall and are rigid via anabelian algorithms; Frobenius-like structures (abstract monoids) are not so rigidified, which allows such filters to be constructed; the two play complementary roles with respect to binding to conventional scheme theory (Fig. 3.2), and Kummer theory relates them within a Hodge theater. (iii) Composing the Theta-link qq_v -> Theta_v with the arrows of Fig. 3.1 gives the correspondence qq_v -> {qq_v^{j^2}}_{1<=j<=l*}, a 'modified Theta-link', viewed as an abstract combinatorial Frobenius lifting, a homotopy between the identity qq_v -> qq_v and qq_v -> qq_v^{(l*)^2}; the exponents {j^2} are highly distinguished (Remark 2.6.3). (iv) Grothendieck Conjecture-type results in anabelian geometry are comparison isomorphisms between polynomial-function-theoretic and group-theoretic collections of morphisms, obtained by combining considerations particular to the situation with Galois evaluation via Kummer theory of polynomial functions or differential forms at rational points.
IUT2.Rem3_6_2.conclusion: Interpretation of the diagram of Corollary 3.6 (ii): Kummer, Galois evaluation and forgetting as in Fig. 3.1; the complementary roles of etale-like and Frobenius-like structures; the modified Theta-link qq_v -> {qq_v^{j^2}}_{1<=j<=l*} as a homotopy between the identity and qq_v -> qq_v^{(l*)^2}; Grothendieck Conjecture-type results as comparison isomorphisms.
obligations: Interpretive; no mathematical claim beyond Corollary 3.6 and the cited results. The objects (Theta-link, Gaussian monoids) have no Lean vocabulary.

IUT2.Rem2_5_1.frag.theta_series_quasi_pe.content: The theta series Theta(u) = sum over n in Z of (-1)^n r^(n(n+1)) u^(2n+1), which is the series of EtTh Proposition 1.4 with q_X = r^2 (since (1/2)(n+1/2)^2 - 1/8 = n(n+1)/2), satisfies Theta(r^a u) = (-1)^a r^(-a^2) u^(-2a) Theta(u) for a in Z; also Theta(u) = -Theta(u^(-1)) and Theta(-u) = -Theta(u); the series is summable for u nonzero when 0 < |r| < 1.
explicit_hypotheses: K a normed field (complete for the summability lemmas)
r in K, r nonzero
u in K, u nonzero
a an integer
0 < |r| < 1 (summability lemmas only)
IUT2.Rem2_5_1.frag.theta_series_quasi_pe.conclusion: thetaSeries r (r^a * u) = (-1)^a * r^(-a^2) * u^(-2a) * thetaSeries r u; thetaSeries r u = -thetaSeries r u^(-1); thetaSeries r (-u) = -thetaSeries r u; Summable (thetaTerm r u).
IUT2.Rem2_5_1.frag.theta_series_quasi_pe.covers: Page 73: the functional equations of [EtTh] Proposition 1.4 (ii) (EtTh page 20, all three displays) from which the values at the points separated by periods from +-sqrt(-1) are computed.

IUT2.Rem2_5_1.frag.theta_series_quasi_pe.scope: classical theta series evaluated at points of a complete normed field; not the etale theta function

IUT2.Rem1_12_2.i.content: (i) Granting the multiradiality of the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism of Corollary 1.10, the essential content of the multiradiality of Corollary 1.12 (the page's wording; not of the whole corollary) lies in the functorial group-theoretic algorithm implicit in the proof of [EtTh] Theorem 1.10 (i) that constructs theta(Pi) up to a mu_{2l}-indeterminacy (rather than only up to an O_k^x-indeterminacy as in the proof of [EtTh] Theorem 1.6 (iii)), together with the elementary observation that the 2l-torsion submodule of any isomorph of O_k^x is characteristic. This content implies that the splittings (dagger_{mu theta})(Pi) are compatible with gluing together the collections of coric data G acting on O^{x mu}(G) arising from distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures.
explicit_hypotheses: The multiradiality of the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism of Corollary 1.10 (the remark works modulo it)
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Corollary 1.12, with Gamma^{x mu} = Ism
IUT2.Rem1_12_2.i.conclusion: The construction of theta(Pi) up to mu_{2l} together with the characteristic nature of the 2l-torsion of O_k^x implies that the splittings (dagger_{mu theta})(Pi) are compatible with gluing the coric data G acting on O^{x mu}(G) from distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures.
obligations: Commentary on the proof of Corollary 1.12 (iii); a formalization of that part would have to prove the stated implication: that mu_{2l}-normalized theta classes plus the characteristic 2l-torsion yield splittings compatible with the Ism-indeterminacy of the coric data.
ambiguities: Page 58: the remark cites 'Corollary 1.12, (b)', but Corollary 1.12 has parts (i) to (iii) and no item (b); possibly a misprint for Corollary 1.10 (b) or for the proof of Corollary 1.12 (iii).

IUT2.Rem3_8_2.ii.content: (ii) Passing by [IUTchI] Proposition 6.7 to the local portion at v in V^bad of a D-Theta NF-Hodge theater removes the label 0 in |F_l| and identifies it with F_l^*, the assignment of D-prime-strips sending 0 and the succeeding label to the one indexed by F_l^*; at the level of the local Frobenioids at v in V^bad (copies of Pi_v acting on O^{triangleright}_{F_v}) attached to these labels this corresponds to the isomorphisms Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_0 -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{<F_l^*>} and (Psi_{dagger C_v})_0 -> (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{<F_l^*>} of Corollaries 3.5 (iii), 3.6 (iii). The resulting situation has an F_l^*-symmetry ([IUTchI] Proposition 4.9 (i)), suited to relating Section 3 at bad v to good v and to the global theory of [IUTchI] Section 5, which relates the multiplicative and additive structures of a number field; one may form processions indexed by subsets of F_l^* ([IUTchI] Proposition 4.11 (i), (ii)), compatible with the |F_l|-processions of (i) ([IUTchI] Proposition 6.9 (iii)).
explicit_hypotheses: v in V^bad
the D-Theta NF-Hodge theater obtained via [IUTchI] Proposition 6.7 from a D-Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theater
IUT2.Rem3_8_2.ii.conclusion: At bad v, passing to a D-Theta NF-Hodge theater corresponds to the two monoid isomorphisms Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_0 -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{<F_l^*>} (Corollary 3.5 (iii)) and (Psi_{dagger C_v})_0 -> (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{<F_l^*>} (Corollary 3.6 (iii)); the resulting situation has an F_l^*-symmetry, and the F_l^*-processions formed from it are compatible with the |F_l|-processions of (i).
obligations: Nothing to formalize.

IUT2.Cor1_12.i.content: (i) There is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm that assigns to Pi a collection of pairs (iota, D): iota is a Delta_Y(Pi)-outer automorphism of Pi_Y(Pi), where Delta_Y(Pi) := Pi_Y(Pi) intersected with Delta, and D is a Delta_Y(Pi)-conjugacy class of closed subgroups of Pi_Y(Pi). For Pi = Pi^tp_{X_k} the collection coincides with the pointed inversion automorphisms of Remark 1.4.1 (ii). If iota induces an action up to torsion on a subset of an abelian group, a superscript iota denotes the elements whose image modulo torsion is fixed.
explicit_hypotheses: The setting of Corollary 1.12
IUT2.Cor1_12.i.conclusion: A functorial group-theoretic algorithm Pi -> {(iota, D)}(Pi) exists and recovers the pointed inversion automorphisms for Pi = Pi^tp_{X_k}.
obligations: No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.
Proof (page 58): follows immediately from Remark 1.4.1 and the references quoted there.

IUT2.Cor1_12.ii.content: (ii) For a pointed inversion automorphism (iota, D), restriction to D gives a commutative square from {M^x_TM . infinity-theta(Pi)}^iota to M^x_TM(Pi) (inside the limit of H^1(J, (l . Delta_Theta)(Pi))) and from {M^x_TM . infinity-theta_env(M^Theta_*(Pi))}^iota to M^x_TM(M^Theta_*(Pi)), the vertical maps being the isomorphisms from the cyclotomic rigidity of Corollary 1.10. The inverse images of the torsion submodules M^mu_TM are infinity-theta(Pi)^iota and infinity-theta_env(M^Theta_*(Pi))^iota. This gives a functorial algorithm for splittings (dagger_{mu theta})(Pi): M^{x mu}_TM(Pi) x {infinity-theta(Pi)^iota / M^mu_TM(Pi)} and the analogous product for M^Theta_*(Pi), that is, direct product decompositions of the images of the iota-invariant subsets in the quotients of the inductive limits by M^mu_TM.
explicit_hypotheses: (iota, D) is a pointed inversion automorphism associated to Pi as in (i)
IUT2.Cor1_12.ii.conclusion: Restriction to D yields the commutative diagram and the splittings (dagger_{mu theta})(Pi), by a functorial algorithm in the topological group Pi.
obligations: No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.
Proof (page 58): follows immediately from the structure of the objects as described in [EtTh] Proposition 1.5, Theorems 1.6, 1.10.

IUT2.Cor1_12.iii.content: (iii) The assignment sending (Pi acting on Pi_mu(M^Theta_*(Pi)) tensor Q/Z, G acting on O^{x mu}(G), alpha_{mu, x mu}) to the data M^Theta_*(Pi), the subsets (dagger_{x theta})(Pi), the splittings (dagger_{mu theta})(Pi), and the diagram (dagger_{mu, x mu}): Pi_mu(M^Theta_*(Pi)) tensor Q/Z -> M^mu_TM(M^Theta_*(Pi)) -> M^mu_TM(Pi) -> M^{x mu}_TM(Pi) -> O^{x mu}(G) determines a functor R -> F arising from a functorial algorithm. The first map is the isomorphism from the injection of Remark 1.5.2, the second comes from the vertical arrows of (dagger_{x theta})(Pi), the third is the trivial homomorphism, and the last is the poly-isomorphism induced by alpha_x of Example 1.8 (iii). With graph R^dagger, the natural functor Psi_R: R -> R^dagger is multiradially defined.
explicit_hypotheses: The setting of Corollary 1.12, with Gamma^{x mu} = Ism
IUT2.Cor1_12.iii.conclusion: Psi_R: R -> R^dagger is multiradially defined.
obligations: No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.

Proof (page 58): the multiradiality follows immediately from the characteristic nature of the torsion submodules M^mu_TM(-). A formalization needs: the torsion submodule is preserved by every isomorphism, so the splitting is compatible with the Ism-indeterminacy on O^{x mu}(G); and the composite through the trivial homomorphism makes the coric data independent of the radial data.
ambiguities: The map M^mu_TM(Pi) -> M^{x mu}_TM(Pi) is called the trivial homomorphism (page 58); it is not the quotient map restricted to torsion in any other sense, which is consistent since M^{x mu}_TM is the quotient by the torsion.

IUT2.Rem1_11_6.content: Cyclotomic rigidity is compared to p-adic Teichmuller theory: the absolute p-adic anabelian result on canonical curves ([CanLift] Theorem 3.6) depends on a cyclotomic rigidity result ([AbsAnab] Lemma 2.5 (ii)); both theories treat cyclotomes as skeleta of arithmetic holomorphic structures, like S^1 inside C^x.
IUT2.Rem1_11_6.conclusion: Cyclotomic rigidity is compared to p-adic Teichmuller theory: the absolute p-adic anabelian result on canonical curves ([CanLift] Theorem 3.6) depends on a cyclotomic rigidity result ([AbsAnab] Lemma 2.5 (ii)); both theories treat cyclotomes as skeleta of arithmetic holomorphic structures, like S^1 inside C^x.
obligations: Nothing to formalize.

IUT2.Rem1_12_2.ii.content: (ii) The algorithm of [EtTh] Theorem 1.10 (i) normalizes the etale theta functions by requiring their values at points over the 2-torsion point mu_- of [IUTchI] Example 4.4 (i) to lie in mu_{2l} (etale theta functions of standard type). The decomposition groups of these points are reconstructed with, among other tools, the elliptic cuspidalizations of Proposition 1.6 (ii).

The decomposition groups of these points are reconstructed with, among other tools, the elliptic cuspidalizations of Proposition 1.6 (ii).

IUT2.Rem1_12_2.iii.content: (iii) If the normalization instead required certain values to equal, for instance, 2 := 1 + 1 in O_k^x inside (k^x)^ (the residue characteristic of k being odd), an element whose construction uses the ring structure of a specific Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater, the normalization would not give a multiradially defined functor, though it would still give a uniradially defined one.
IUT2.Rem1_12_2.iii.conclusion: (iii) If the normalization instead required certain values to equal, for instance, 2 := 1 + 1 in O_k^x inside (k^x)^ (the residue characteristic of k being odd), an element whose construction uses the ring structure of a specific Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater, the normalization would not give a multiradially defined functor, though it would still give a uniradially defined one.

IUT2.Rem1_12_2.iv.content: (iv) For the use of log-shells ([AbsTopIII]) in IUT III, log-shells sit in O^{x mu}(G); an indeterminacy up to a subgroup of O_k^x larger than torsion (for instance generated by 2 and its Aut(G)-conjugates) would force working with the quotient of O^{x mu}(G) by that subgroup, which is not acceptable for the later theory. Hence splittings up to a mu-indeterminacy are needed.

As X double underline -> X is totally ramified at the cusps, each map of dual graphs of special fibers induced by the coverings of Proposition 2.1 is a bijection on vertices. (ii) With the inversion automorphisms of Remark 1.4.1, Gamma^{black-triangle}_X is the unique connected subtree of Gamma_X stabilized by iota_X containing every vertex, and Gamma^bullet_X the unique stabilized subgraph with exactly one vertex and no edges; labeling vertices by -l^*, ..., l^* with 0 fixed, Gamma^{black-triangle} drops the edge joining +-l^*, and Gamma^bullet is the vertex 0. (iii) Passing between distinct v through this bridge, the groups Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot} do not globalize, which is why the conjugacy indeterminacies on conjugates of I_t and of Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot} are independent; since neither Pi-hat^+-_v -> G_v nor Pi^{circledcirc +-} -> G_K has a section normalizing all I_t, a G_v- or G_K-conjugacy indeterminacy yields a Delta-hat^+-_v-conjugacy indeterminacy; since Delta-hat^cor_v -> Delta-hat^cor_v / Delta-hat^+-_v does not split, the outer action of F_l^{x+-} induces independent indeterminacies on the I_t for distinct t; and since G_v is not a direct summand of G_K, a G_K-conjugacy indeterminacy induces independent G_v-conjugacy indeterminacies. IUT2.Rem2_6_1.content: (i) A central property of the evaluation algorithm of Corollary 2.5 (iii) is that it is performed relative to a single basepoint, the group Pi^gamma_{v black-triangle-double-dot} of the connected subgraph Gamma^{black-triangle}_X; so the theta values theta^{|t|} for the various |t| are all computed relative to a single copy of G_v(Pi^gamma_{v black-triangle-double-dot}) and a single cyclotome (l . Delta_Theta), independent of |t|. This is called conjugate synchronization, and it is needed for the Kummer theory of Section 3. (ii) For Gaussian Frobenioids this means the theta values for |t| in F_l^* are treated as a single entity whose Kummer theory uses one Galois group and one cyclotome acting simultaneously on N-th roots of all the values, compatibly with the base field; this requires a single basepoint of a connected geometric object, and the Kummer-theoretic representation of the monoid generated by the theta function is compatible with the log-wall, which is used in IUT III.

IUT2.Rem2_6_2.content: (i) In terms of D-Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theaters ([IUTchI] Definition 6.4 (iii)), one may view Pi_v as the tempered group of dagger D_{>,v}, Pi-hat^+-_v as the commensurator of the closure of Pi_v in the profinite group of dagger D^{circledcirc +-} via the zero-labeled portions of the bridges, and the outer action of Delta-hat^cor_v / Delta-hat^+-_v = F_l^{x+-} as the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry of [IUTchI] Proposition 6.8 (i). Then the single basepoint of conjugate synchronization is compatible with the single basepoint of label synchronization ([IUTchI] Remark 6.12.4), so conjugate synchronization is compatible with the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry; this compatibility is essentially Corollary 2.4 (iii). (ii) This contrasts with the incompatibility with the F_l^*-symmetry of [IUTchI] Proposition 4.9 (i) for D-Theta NF-Hodge theaters, which permutes multiple copies of local objects at the expense of label crushing. (iii) The F_l^{x+-}-symmetry, unlike the F_l^*-symmetry, allows comparison with the label zero, hence with the copies of O_k^x in the splittings of Corollary 1.12 (ii) giving constant multiple rigidity; this is the content of Corollary 2.6.

IUT2.Rem2_8_3.content: (i) Using the archimedean line segment Gamma^{black-triangle}_X to single out representatives in {-l^*, ..., l^*} (absolute value at most l^*) of the nonarchimedean classes modulo l recalls computing global sections of an arithmetic line bundle ([Szp] pages 13 to 14) and the arithmetic of the graph of the loop Gamma_X ([SemiAnbd] Remark 1.5.1). (ii) This use of a connected archimedean segment depends on the discreteness of Z, an application of the discrete rigidity of [EtTh]; in Corollary 2.8 it is closely tied to cyclotomic rigidity, discrete rigidity (discreteness of squares of elements of Z modulo {+-1}) being a dual of the cyclotomic rigidity of (l . Delta_Theta)(-), a duality embodied in the structure and values of the etale theta function ([EtTh] Propositions 1.4 (ii), (iii), 1.5 (ii)). The group-theoretic theta evaluation may similarly be considered relative to the natural isomorphism mu_Zhat(G_k) -> mu_Zhat(Pi_X) of [AbsTopIII] Corollary 1.10 (c).

IUT2.Rem2_9_1.content: (i) The cyclotomic rigidity involving Pi_mu(-) in Corollary 2.8 admits a multiradial formulation (Corollary 1.10), whereas that involving mu_Zhat(G_v(-)) in Corollary 2.9 admits, from the viewpoint of Remark 1.11.3 (iv), only a uniradial one unless the rigidity is sacrificed as in Corollary 1.11. (ii) The advantage of mu_Zhat(G_v(-)) is access to the uniradially defined natural surjection H^1(G_v(-), mu_Zhat(G_v(-))) -> Zhat of Remark 1.11.5. (iii) Hence the algorithms of Corollary 2.9 (ii), (iii) give only uniradially defined functors; IUT III modifies them with log-shells to obtain multiradially defined ones at the cost of mild indeterminacies.

IUT2.Prop3_1.content: Mono-theta-theoretic theta monoids. Let M^Theta_* be a projective system of mono-theta environments with Pi_X(M^Theta_*) isomorphic to Pi_v (abbreviated M^Theta_* inside parentheses). (i) Split theta monoids: by Proposition 1.5 (iii) and Corollary 2.8 (i) there is a functorial algorithm M^Theta_* -> {M^x_TM(M^Theta_*), theta^iota_env, infinity-theta^iota_env, M^x_TM . infinity-theta^iota_env within the limit over finite index open J of H^1(Pi_Y(M^Theta_*)|_J, Pi_mu(M^Theta_*))}_iota, iota ranging over the inversion automorphisms of Proposition 2.2 (i), with a natural conjugation action by Pi_X(M^Theta_*); hence an algorithm for the theta monoids Psi_env(M^Theta_*) := {Psi^iota_env = M^x_TM . theta^iota_env(M^Theta_*)^N}_iota and infinity-Psi_env := {M^x_TM . infinity-theta^iota_env(M^Theta_*)^N}_iota (submonoids of the direct limit of cohomology modules), and for their splittings up to torsion determined by M^x_TM, theta^iota_env, infinity-theta^iota_env (Corollary 2.8 (iii)). (ii) Constant monoids: using the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms of Corollaries 2.8 (i), 2.9 and the inverse image of Z within Zhat under the surjection of Remark 1.11.5 (i) for G_v(M^Theta_*), there is a functorial algorithm M^Theta_* -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*) := M_TM(M^Theta_*) within the same limit of H^1 with Pi_mu coefficients, a monoid of constants naturally isomorphic to O^{triangleright}_{F_v} (Example 1.8 (ii)), with a conjugation action by Pi_X(M^Theta_*).
explicit_hypotheses: M^Theta_* = {... -> M^Theta_{M'} -> M^Theta_M -> ...} a projective system of mono-theta environments (Proposition 1.5, Corollary 2.8) with Pi_X(M^Theta_*) isomorphic to Pi_v
IUT2.Prop3_1.conclusion: (i) a functorial algorithm for the theta monoids Psi_env(M^Theta_*), infinity-Psi_env(M^Theta_*) and their splittings up to torsion; (ii) a functorial algorithm for the constant monoid Psi_cns(M^Theta_*), with conjugation actions by Pi_X(M^Theta_*).

Theta_v^N|_{A} within infinity-Psi := O^x . Theta_v^{Q>=0}|_{A} within O^x(T_{A^Theta_infinity}) (Q>=0 meaning some positive power equals a positive power of Theta_v), and, for conjugates Theta^alpha_v, submonoids Psi_{F^Theta_v, alpha}; Pi_v surjects onto Aut(Y-double-dot) and acts by conjugation on the collections Psi_{F^Theta_v} := {Psi_{F^Theta_v, alpha}}_{alpha in Pi_v}, infinity-Psi likewise; Theta^{Q>=0} determines characteristic splittings up to torsion compatible with Pi_v; this data is reconstructible category-theoretically from F_v up to inner automorphisms of Pi_v. (ii) The base-field-theoretic hull C_v of F_v gives a monoid O^{triangleright}_{C_v}(-) and, on A^Theta_infinity, a monoid Psi_{C_v} with a Pi_v-action, also reconstructible category-theoretically from F_v up to inner automorphisms.

IUT2.Prop3_3.content: Frobenioid-theoretic theta monoids. Suppose, in the situation of Proposition 3.1, that M^Theta_* = M^Theta_*(dagger F_v) arises (Proposition 1.2 (ii)) from a tempered Frobenioid dagger F_v appearing in a Theta-Hodge theater ([IUTchI] Definition 3.6). The constructions of Example 3.2 give Pi_X(M^Theta_*) acting on Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v} = {Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v, alpha}}, infinity-Psi likewise, and on Psi_{dagger C_v}, with splittings up to torsion. (i) Split theta monoids: forming Kummer classes relative to the Frobenioid structure (extracting N-th roots for N >= 1) and using Proposition 1.3 (i) for the exterior cyclotome, one obtains, for a suitable bijection of l.Z-torsors between Gal(Y/Y)-orbits of iota and images of alpha under Pi_v -> l.Z, collections of isomorphisms Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v, alpha} -> Psi^iota_env(M^Theta_*) and infinity versions, each defined up to an inner automorphism and compatible with the conjugation actions and the splittings; written Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v} -> Psi_env(M^Theta_*). (ii) Constant monoids: likewise an isomorphism Psi_{dagger C_v} -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*), defined up to an inner automorphism and compatible with the conjugation actions.
explicit_hypotheses: The situation of Proposition 3.1
M^Theta_* = M^Theta_*(dagger F_v) for a tempered Frobenioid dagger F_v in a Theta-Hodge theater
IUT2.Prop3_3.conclusion: Kummer isomorphisms Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v} -> Psi_env(M^Theta_*) (with infinity versions) and Psi_{dagger C_v} -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*), each up to an inner automorphism, compatible with conjugation actions and splittings.

IUT2.Prop3_4.content: Group-theoretic theta monoids. Let dagger F_v be as in Proposition 3.3 and consider the full poly-isomorphism M^Theta_*(Pi_v) -> M^Theta_*(dagger F_v) of projective systems of mono-theta environments (M^Theta_*(Pi_v) from Proposition 1.2 (i)). (i) Multiradiality of split theta monoids: each isomorphism induces compatible diagrams of isomorphisms Pi_v -> Pi_X(...) acting on infinity-Psi_env(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)) -> infinity-Psi_env(M^Theta_*(dagger F_v)) -> infinity-Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v} (and on Psi_env), and G_v acting on the unit groups Psi_env(...)^x -> (Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v})^x, compatible with splittings up to torsion; with (Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v})^{x mu} the quotient of the units by torsion, the functorial algorithms Pi_v -> Psi_env(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)), infinity-Psi_env (composing Propositions 1.2 (i), 3.1 (i)) are compatible with arbitrary automorphisms of the pair G_v(M^Theta_*(dagger F_v)) acting on (Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v})^{x mu} that are Ism-multiples of automorphisms induced by automorphisms of the pair with (Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v})^x, so that Psi_R of Corollary 1.12 (iii) is multiradially defined. (ii) Uniradiality of constant monoids: each isomorphism induces analogous diagrams for Psi_cns and Psi_{dagger C_v}, but the algorithm Pi_v -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)) depends on the cyclotomic rigidity of Corollary 1.11 (b) (through the surjection of Remark 1.11.5 (i) used in Proposition 3.1 (ii)), hence fails to be compatible with automorphisms of the pair G_v acting on (Psi_{dagger C_v})^{x mu} that arise from automorphisms of the pair with (Psi_{dagger C_v})^x; it only admits a uniradial formulation.
explicit_hypotheses: dagger F_v a tempered Frobenioid as in Proposition 3.3
an isomorphism of projective systems of mono-theta environments M^Theta_*(Pi_v) -> M^Theta_*(dagger F_v)
IUT2.Prop3_4.conclusion: (i) The split theta monoid algorithms are compatible with Ism-multiples of automorphisms of the unit pair, so the theta monoids are multiradially defined; (ii) the constant monoid algorithm is not compatible with such automorphisms and only admits a uniradial formulation.

Subscript |t| denotes identifying the copies labeled t and -t; <|F_l|> (respectively <F_l^*>) denotes the diagonal embedding into the product of copies over |t| in |F_l| (respectively F_l^*). Restricting Psi_cns(M^Theta_*) via the restrictions of Corollary 2.8 (i), (ii) gives compatible morphisms Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot}(M^Theta_{* black-triangle-double-dot}) -> G_v(...)_{<|F_l|>} acting on Psi_cns(M^Theta_*) -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{<|F_l|>}, the bottom arrow an isomorphism of monoids, compatible with the symmetrizing isomorphisms and defined up to an inner automorphism of Pi_X(M^Theta_*); this inner automorphism indeterminacy, a priori depending on |t|, is independent of |t| in |F_l|.

Each Gaussian monoid carries a natural action of G_v(M^Theta_{* black-triangle-double-dot})_{<F_l^*>}. The submonoid Psi_{2l . xi} generated by Psi^x_cns_{<F_l^*>} and xi^{2l . N} is independent of xi. IUT2.Rem4_8_2.content: (i) The realified localization functor of Remark 4.8.1 (iii) concerns only the realification of F_gau(dagger HT^Theta); the unit portion of the Gaussian monoids is used in the log-wall theory of IUT III as an additive object via log, the non-realified global Frobenioids of Corollary 4.8 (i) serving as a translation apparatus between multiplicative and additive line bundles (Remark 4.7.2); this depends essentially on the natural splittings of the Gaussian monoids (Corollary 4.6 (iv); Remark 1.12.2 (iv)). (ii) That these non-realified Frobenioids appear only with the F_l^*-symmetry (Remark 4.7.6) is no obstacle, since Gaussian monoids are naturally functions of j in F_l^* (Remark 4.7.3 (iii)). (iii) In the analogy with p-adic Teichmuller theory ([AbsTopIII] Section I5), log-shifted units with non-log-shifted value groups resemble writing an indigenous bundle with Hodge filtration 0 -> omega -> E -> tau -> 0 as a direct sum Phi^* tau + omega under Frobenius liftings, Phi corresponding to log.

(ii): C a category equivalent to the tempered Frobenioid determined by X_k

IUT2.Def1_1.content: Setting of Section 1 (page 20): N a positive integer, l an odd prime, k an MLF of odd residue characteristic p != l containing a primitive 4l-th root of unity, X double underline_k a hyperbolic curve of type (1, (Z/lZ)^Theta) over k with stable model over O_k, C_k its k-core, Pi^tp the tempered fundamental group, G_k = Gal(kbar/k), Delta^tp the geometric tempered fundamental group. Let M^Theta be a mod N mono-theta environment ([EtTh] Definition 2.13 (ii)) isomorphic to the mod N model mono-theta environment of X double underline_k, with underlying topological group Pi_{M^Theta}. (i) There are functorial algorithms producing from M^Theta: a quotient Pi_{M^Theta} -> Pi_Y(M^Theta) (Y double underline); a topological group Pi_X(M^Theta) (X double underline) isomorphic to Pi^tp of X double underline_k containing Pi_Y(M^Theta) as a normal open subgroup; a quotient Pi_X(M^Theta) -> G(M^Theta) corresponding to G_k; the kernels Delta_{M^Theta}, Delta_Y(M^Theta), Delta_X(M^Theta) of the maps to G(M^Theta); a subquotient (l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta) of Pi_Y(M^Theta) with a natural Pi_X(M^Theta)-action, abstractly isomorphic to Zhat(1); and a closed normal subgroup Pi_mu(M^Theta) = Ker(Pi_{M^Theta} -> Pi_Y(M^Theta)) with a natural Pi_X(M^Theta)-action, abstractly isomorphic to (Z/NZ)(1). The structure of M^Theta determines a lifting of the natural outer action of (l . Z)(M^Theta) := Pi_X(M^Theta)/Pi_Y(M^Theta), isomorphic to Delta_X(M^Theta)/Delta_Y(M^Theta), on Delta_Y(M^Theta) to an outer action on Delta_{M^Theta}. (ii) (l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta) and Pi_mu(M^Theta) are called the interior and exterior cyclotomes; by [EtTh] Corollary 2.19 (i) there is a functorial algorithm constructing a cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta) tensor Z/NZ -> Pi_mu(M^Theta).
explicit_hypotheses: N a positive integer; l an odd prime
k an MLF of odd residue characteristic p != l containing a primitive 4l-th root of unity; kbar an algebraic closure of k
X double underline_k a hyperbolic curve of type (1, (Z/lZ)^Theta) over k ([EtTh] Definition 2.5 (i)) admitting a stable model over O_k; C_k its k-core
M^Theta a mod N mono-theta environment ([EtTh] Definition 2.13 (ii)) isomorphic to the mod N model mono-theta environment determined by X double underline_k
IUT2.Def1_1.conclusion: (i) Functorial algorithms M^Theta -> Pi_Y(M^Theta), Pi_X(M^Theta), G(M^Theta), Delta_{M^Theta}, Delta_Y(M^Theta), Delta_X(M^Theta), (l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta), Pi_mu(M^Theta) with the stated properties, and a lifting of the outer action of (l . Z)(M^Theta) on Delta_Y(M^Theta) to Delta_{M^Theta}; (ii) the names interior and exterior cyclotome, and a functorial algorithm for the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta) tensor Z/NZ -> Pi_mu(M^Theta).

IUT2.Rem1_4_1.content: Recollection from [EtTh] Sections 1, 2 of the theory of etale theta functions of standard type. (i) X double underline_k -> X single underline_k -> C single underline_k are the hyperbolic orbicurves of type (1, l-tors), (1, l-tors)_+- determined by X double underline_k ([EtTh] Proposition 2.4); X single underline_k has a unique zero cusp, fixed by Gal(X_k/C_k); mu_- in X single underline_k(k) is the unique torsion point of order 2 whose closure in any stable model over O_k meets the same irreducible component of the special fiber as the zero cusp. (ii) The unique order two automorphism iota of X double underline_k over k lies over an order two automorphism of X single underline_k and corresponds to the unique order two Delta^tp-outer automorphism of Pi^tp over G_k. Y-double-dot_k -> Y_k -> X_k (double underlines) are the tempered coverings for the open subgroups of Proposition 1.4 and Definition 1.1 (i), Proposition 1.2 (i). Since k contains a primitive 4l-th root of unity, there are rational points (mu_-)_{Y-double-dot} and (mu_-)_X over mu_-; iota fixes the Gal(X double underline/X single underline)-orbit of (mu_-)_X, hence (as l != 2 and Aut is Z/2lZ) fixes (mu_-)_X; so there is an order two automorphism iota_{Y-double-dot} lifting iota, unique up to l . Z-conjugacy and composition with Gal(Y-double-dot/Y), fixing the Gal(Y-double-dot/Y)-orbit of some point of the Gal(Y-double-dot/X)-orbit of (mu_-)_{Y-double-dot}. These are the inversion automorphisms; D_{mu_-} in Pi^tp of Y-double-dot double underline is the decomposition group of (mu_-)_{Y-double-dot}, well defined up to conjugacy by Delta^tp of Y-double-dot double underline, and determined by iota_{Y-double-dot} up to conjugacy by Delta^tp_{Y_k} := Delta_Y(M^Theta(Pi^tp of X double underline_k)) (Y without underline, notation of Remark 1.1.1 (i)); either pair (iota, point) or (iota as outer automorphism, D_{mu_-}) is a pointed inversion automorphism. An etale theta function of standard type is defined precisely by the condition that its restriction to D_{mu_-} is a 2l-th root of unity ([EtTh] Definition 1.9 (ii), Definition 2.7).

IUT2.Prop1_5.content: Projective systems of mono-theta environments. Let M^Theta_* = {... -> M^Theta_{M'} -> M^Theta_M -> ...} be a projective system of mono-theta environments, M^Theta_M a mod M mono-theta environment isomorphic to the mod M model one of X double underline_k, M varying multiplicatively in N_{>=1}. (i) Such a system is uniquely determined up to isomorphism by X double underline_k (discrete rigidity, [EtTh] Corollary 2.19 (ii)). (ii) The transition morphisms of the system {Pi_X(M^Theta_M)} (X double underline) are all isomorphisms; any isomorphism Pi_X(M^Theta_{M'}) -> Pi_X(M^Theta_M), M dividing M', lifts to a morphism of mono-theta environments; identifying along them gives Pi_X(M^Theta_*), with open subgroup Pi_{Y-double-dot}(M^Theta_*), subquotient (l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta_*) and quotient G(M^Theta_*). (iii) The exterior cyclotomes form a projective system with limit Pi_mu(M^Theta_*), with a uniquely determined cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta_*) -> Pi_mu(M^Theta_*) (from those of Definition 1.1 (ii)); transporting theta(Pi) of Proposition 1.4 gives a functorial algorithm M^Theta_* -> theta_env(M^Theta_*) in H^1(Pi_{Y-double-dot}(M^Theta_*), Pi_mu(M^Theta_*)), and infinity-theta_env(M^Theta_*) in the direct limit over finite index open J of H^1(Pi_{Y-double-dot}(M^Theta_*)|_J, Pi_mu(M^Theta_*)) is the set of elements some positive multiple of which coincides up to torsion with an element of theta_env(M^Theta_*). (iv) If M^Theta_* arises from a tempered Frobenioid C (Propositions 1.2 (ii), 1.3), the construction of theta_env(M^Theta_*) is compatible with the Kummer-theoretic construction of the etale theta function from the Frobenioid-theoretic theta function, in particular with the Kummer theory of the base-field-theoretic hull C^{bs-fld}.

M^Theta_* a projective system of mono-theta environments M^Theta_M, each mod M and isomorphic to the mod M model mono-theta environment of X double underline_k, M varying multiplicatively in N_{>=1}

IUT2.Rem1_5_1.conclusion: Discrete rigidity makes projective systems of mono-theta environments compatible with the discrete structure given by the isomorphs of N in tempered Frobenioids.

IUT2.Prop1_6.content: Cores and cuspidalizations. Let Pi be as in Proposition 1.2 (i) and Delta the group-theoretic subgroup of Pi corresponding to Delta^tp of X double underline_k ([AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.8). (i) (Cores) There is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm ([AbsTopII] Corollary 3.3 (i), Remark 3.3.3) constructing from Pi a topological group Pi_C(Pi) with an augmentation Pi_C(Pi) -> Pi/Delta (kernel Delta_C(Pi)) that contains Pi as an open subgroup compatibly with the surjections to Pi/Delta, such that for Pi = Pi^tp of X double underline_k the inclusion Pi in Pi_C(Pi) is naturally identified with Pi^tp of X double underline_k in Pi^tp of C_k. (ii) (Elliptic cuspidalizations) For a positive integer N there is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm ([AbsTopII] Corollary 3.3 (iii), Remark 3.3.3) constructing Pi_{U_N}(Pi) with a surjection Pi_{U_N}(Pi) -> Pi such that for Pi = Pi^tp it is naturally identified with the elliptic cuspidalization arising from an open immersion determined by the N-torsion points of a once-punctured elliptic curve forming a double covering of C_k.

Delta in Pi the subgroup corresponding to the geometric tempered fundamental group
For (ii): N a positive integer

IUT2.Rem1_1_1.iv.content: (iv) The isomorphism admits a symmetry for Delta_C(M^Theta)/Delta_X(M^Theta) (X single underline), isomorphic to F_l^{x+-} ([IUTchI] Definition 6.1 (v)). The conjugation action of Pi_Y(M^Theta) (Y double underline) on Pi_{M^Theta}|_{(l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta)} factors through G(M^Theta), so via Pi_C(M^Theta) -> G(M^Theta) one has a naively defined Pi_C(M^Theta)-action. The model for Pi_{M^Theta} is the subgroup Pi_mu(M^Theta) semidirect Pi_Y(M^Theta) (Y double underline) of Pi_mu(M^Theta) semidirect Pi_C(M^Theta); the subquotient Pi_mu semidirect (l . Delta_Theta) is stabilized by conjugation, and that action factors through G(M^Theta) and is the action via the cyclotomic character. So the naively defined action coincides with the conjugation action from the model embedding, even without the embedding. The inclusion Delta_X (double) in Delta_X (single) induces isomorphisms Delta_X(double)/Delta_Y(double) -> Delta_X(single)/Delta_Y(no underline) and Delta^ell_Y(double) -> Delta^ell_Y(no underline), whose codomains are stabilized by Pi_C(M^Theta); the commutator map becomes (Delta_X(single)/Delta_Y) x Delta^ell_Y -> Pi_{M^Theta}|_{(l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta)}, a map between sets with natural Pi_C(M^Theta)-actions, and it is Pi_C(M^Theta)-equivariant; the subgroups of (iii) are stabilized by Pi_C(M^Theta). The model embedding is reconstructible algorithmically from M^Theta up to composition with automorphisms of Pi_{M^Theta} differing from the identity by a twisted homomorphism Pi_{M^Theta} -> Pi_Y(M^Theta) (Y double underline) -> Pi^ell_Y(M^Theta) -> Pi_mu(M^Theta) arising from a Kummer class of a product of integral powers of (U-double-dot)^2 and q_X^{l/2} ([EtTh] Proposition 1.4 (ii)); such automorphisms do not affect the commutator map. Stability under Delta_X(M^Theta) (single underline) is less interesting, being a consequence of functoriality under automorphisms ([EtTh] Corollaries 2.18 (iv), 2.19 (i)); the symmetry of interest is for the quotient Delta_C -> Delta_C/Delta_X, isomorphic to F_l^{x+-}.

IUT2.Rem1_1_1.v.content: (v) The symmetries of mono-theta environments for the conjugation action by Delta_X(M^Theta) (single underline) come from the shifting automorphisms of [EtTh] Proposition 2.14 (ii). The meromorphic theta function itself has no such symmetries, while the mono-theta environment does; this distinguishes mono-theta from bi-theta environments ([EtTh] Remark 2.14.3) and is a fundamental difference between the mono-theta-theoretic approach to cyclotomic rigidity of [EtTh] and the approach of [IUTchI] Example 5.1 (v) via Kummer classes of rational functions, comparable to constructing cyclotomic rigidity from a line bundle (more symmetries) versus from a rational function. Mimicking [EtTh] for the quotient Delta_C -> Delta_C/Delta_X, isomorphic to F_l^{x+-}, requires denominators 1/l in Pi_{M^Theta}|_{(l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta)}; in the commutator map such terms vanish, because Pi_{M^Theta}|_{(l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta)} commutes with the elements involved. This yields the F_l^{x+-}-symmetric cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism of (iv), weaker than the full mono-theta environment (which has F_l^{x+-}-symmetries only with denominators), comparable to constructing cyclotomic rigidity from the curvature (first Chern class) of the line bundle (cf. Remark 3.6.5).

IUT2.Rem1_1_1.v.conclusion: Mono-theta environments, unlike the theta function, admit the shifting symmetries; with denominators 1/l these extend to F_l^{x+-}, and since the denominator terms vanish in the commutator map, the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism is F_l^{x+-}-symmetric without them.
obligations: Page 25: the vanishing of the terms with denominators 1/l in the commutator map is attributed to a commutativity property without a computation. The comparisons with line bundles and first Chern classes are interpretive.
