IUT2.Rem1_6_1.content: The construction of Proposition 1.6 (i) amounts to computing centralizers of the image of open subgroups of Pi/Delta in the outer automorphism groups of open subgroups of Delta; that of Proposition 1.6 (ii) amounts to computing outer isomorphisms between subquotients of Delta compatible with the outer actions of open subgroups of Pi/Delta. Analogous results hold for more general functorial group-theoretic algorithms involving chains of elementary operations ([AbsTopI] Section 4), e.g. Belyi cuspidalizations ([AbsTopII] Corollary 3.7).
IUT2.Rem1_6_1.conclusion: The algorithms of Proposition 1.6 reduce to computing centralizers in outer automorphism groups (cores) and compatible outer isomorphisms between subquotients of Delta (elliptic cuspidalizations); analogous algorithms exist for chains of elementary operations such as Belyi cuspidalizations.
obligations: Page 32: the 'analogous result' for chains of elementary operations is asserted with a reference to [AbsTopI] Section 4 and [AbsTopII] Corollary 3.7 only.

IUT2.Ex1_7.content: Radial and coric data I: generalities. Defines radial and coric data, radial environments (R, C, Phi: R -> C), multiradial and uniradial environments, the tautological multiradialization, the switching functor criterion for multiradiality, multiradially, uniradially and corically defined functors Psi_R, and the interpretation of multiradiality as simultaneous execution compatible with gluing of coric portions, in five parts.
obligations: Parent of the part records; the status of each part is given there.

IUT2.Ex1_7.i.content: (i) A type of mathematical data called radial data (formalized in [IUTchIV] Section 3; thought of as input or output of a functorial algorithm, [IUTchI] Remark 3.2.1) gives a category R whose objects are collections of radial data and whose morphisms are isomorphisms; likewise coric data give a category C of collections of coric data and their isomorphisms. A functorial algorithm, called radial, with input radial data and output coric data, gives a functor Phi: R -> C, assumed essentially surjective; R and Phi are called radial and C coric. For a nonempty index set I one considers copies {Phi_i: R_i -> C}_{i in I} with common codomain C (Fig. 1.1), R_i being radial data equipped with a label i.
explicit_hypotheses: R a category all of whose morphisms are isomorphisms (radial data)
C a category all of whose morphisms are isomorphisms (coric data)
Phi: R -> C a functor arising from a functorial algorithm, assumed essentially surjective
I a nonempty index set (for the labeled copies)
IUT2.Ex1_7.i.conclusion: Definitions of radial data, coric data, the radial functor Phi: R -> C and labeled copies Phi_i: R_i -> C.
obligations: Definitional; R and C are groupoids and Phi an essentially surjective functor, which Mathlib can express; the phrase 'arises from a functorial algorithm' has no formal counterpart outside [IUTchIV] Section 3.
ambiguities: Page 32: 'type of mathematical data' and 'functorial algorithm' are used informally here; the paper points to [IUTchIV] Section 3 for a formalization.

IUT2.Ex1_7.ii.content: (ii) A triple (R, C, Phi: R -> C) as in (i) is a radial environment; it is multiradial if Phi is full, uniradial otherwise. For a uniradial environment an object of R may lose rigidity (gain indeterminacy) when mapped to C; multiradiality means that applying the radial algorithm causes no loss of rigidity. If any two collections of radial data are isomorphic, the tautological multiradialization (R^mtz, C, Phi^mtz) is defined: objects are triples (R, C, alpha) with R in R, C in C and alpha: Phi(R) -> C a full poly-isomorphism; isomorphisms (R, C, alpha) -> (R*, C*, alpha*) are pairs of isomorphisms R -> R*, C -> C* (necessarily compatible with alpha, alpha*); the coric data are those of the original environment and the radial algorithm is (R, C, alpha) -> C, whose functor is full and essentially surjective; there is a natural functor R -> R^mtz, R -> (R, Phi(R), Phi(R) -> Phi(R)). It forgets the uniradiality in a minimal way.
explicit_hypotheses: (R, C, Phi) a radial environment as in (i)
For the multiradialization: any two collections of radial data (objects of R) are isomorphic
IUT2.Ex1_7.ii.conclusion: Definitions of multiradial and uniradial environments; for a radial environment with all objects of R isomorphic, the tautological multiradialization (R^mtz, C, Phi^mtz) is a multiradial environment with a natural functor R -> R^mtz.
obligations: Page 33: that Phi^mtz is full is called clear, from the assumption that any two radial data are isomorphic, and the compatibility of isomorphisms with alpha, alpha* is called necessary; no argument is written. With alpha a full poly-isomorphism (the set of all isomorphisms) these are elementary category-theoretic facts that could be stated in Lean once the multiradialization is defined.
ambiguities: Page 33: an object of R^mtz carries a full poly-isomorphism alpha, i.e. the set of all isomorphisms Phi(R) -> C, not a single isomorphism; the record follows that reading.

IUT2.Ex1_7.iii.content: (iii) Let R x_C R be the category of triples (R1, R2, alpha) with R1, R2 in R and alpha: Phi(R1) -> Phi(R2) an isomorphism, with the evident morphisms ([FrdI] Section 0, categorical fiber product), and sw: R x_C R -> R x_C R the switching functor (R1, R2, alpha) -> (R2, R1, alpha^{-1}). A formal consequence of multiradiality is that sw preserves the isomorphism class of every object; in fact multiradiality is equivalent to every object (R1, R2, alpha) being isomorphic to (R1, R1, id: Phi(R1) -> Phi(R1)), which sw leaves unchanged.
explicit_hypotheses: (R, C, Phi: R -> C) a radial environment
IUT2.Ex1_7.iii.conclusion: (R, C, Phi) is multiradial (Phi full) if and only if every object (R1, R2, alpha) of R x_C R is isomorphic to (R1, R1, id); in particular, for a multiradial environment the switching functor preserves isomorphism classes.
definitions_required: categorical fiber product R x_C R ([FrdI] Section 0)
obligations: Page 34: the equivalence is said to be verified 'immediately'; no argument is written. It is an elementary statement about a functor between categories whose morphisms are isomorphisms and is a candidate for a Lean statement with Mathlib's category theory.
ambiguities: Page 34: 'the evident sense' of morphisms of R x_C R is not spelled out; the natural reading is pairs (f1, f2) of morphisms of R with Phi(f2) . alpha = alpha' . Phi(f1).

IUT2.Ex1_7.iv.content: (iv) Given another radial environment (R^dagger, C^dagger, Phi^dagger) (daggered radial and coric data, daggered radial algorithm) and a 1-commutative square Phi^dagger . Psi_R = Psi_C . Phi with Psi_R: R -> R^dagger and Psi_C: C -> C^dagger arising from functorial algorithms: if (R, C, Phi) is multiradial (respectively uniradial), Psi_R is called multiradially defined (respectively uniradially defined), or multiradial (uniradial). If Psi_R factors (up to 1-isomorphism) as Xi_R . Phi with Xi_R: C -> R^dagger arising from a functorial algorithm, Psi_R is corically defined (coric). The case R = C, Phi = id_R shows that a corically defined Psi_R is a special case of a multiradial one.
explicit_hypotheses: (R, C, Phi) and (R^dagger, C^dagger, Phi^dagger) radial environments
a 1-commutative square with Psi_R: R -> R^dagger, Psi_C: C -> C^dagger arising from functorial algorithms
IUT2.Ex1_7.iv.conclusion: Definitions of multiradially, uniradially and corically defined functors Psi_R.
obligations: Definitional.
ambiguities: Page 34: 'multiradially defined' is a property of the source environment (R, C, Phi), not of Psi_R itself; the definition attaches it to Psi_R.

IUT2.Ex1_7.v.content: (v) If Psi_R is multiradially defined, its multiradiality allows simultaneous execution of the functorial algorithm for Psi_R on collections of radial input data indexed by I (Fig. 1.1), compatibly with identification of their coric portions (via Phi): gluing isomorphisms in C lift to gluing isomorphisms in R, to which Psi_R can be applied, giving gluing isomorphisms of the output data. If Psi_R is uniradial, the output depends a priori on the additional rigidity of objects of R relative to their images in C, so the effect of arbitrary gluing isomorphisms in C on the output cannot be computed.
explicit_hypotheses: The situation of (iv), with Psi_R multiradially defined
IUT2.Ex1_7.v.conclusion: For multiradially defined Psi_R, gluing isomorphisms in C lift to R and hence act on the output of Psi_R; for uniradial Psi_R no such computation is available.
obligations: Interpretive; the mathematical content (lifting of isomorphisms of C to R) is the fullness of Phi of (ii).

IUT2.Rem1_7_1.content: The fullness condition in the definition of a multiradial environment allows parallel transport between fibers of the radial functor Phi: R -> C (lifting isomorphisms in C to isomorphisms in R, Example 1.7 (iv), (v)); such liftings are unique up to an indeterminacy arising from the failure of Phi to be faithful. A uniradial environment is an abstraction of a fibration without a connection, a multiradial environment of a fibration with a connection, the coric data being the horizontal part of the radial data.
implicit_hypotheses: A radial environment (R, C, Phi) as in Example 1.7
IUT2.Rem1_7_1.conclusion: Fullness of Phi lets isomorphisms of C lift to R, uniquely up to the indeterminacy coming from non-faithfulness of Phi; multiradial environments are analogous to fibrations with a connection.
obligations: The uniqueness of liftings up to the non-faithfulness of Phi is called a tautological observation; the fibration and connection analogy is interpretive and has no formal content.

IUT2.Rem1_8_1.content: In the examples of Example 1.8 (iii) to (ix): no automorphism of O^{x mu}(G) induced by an element of Aut(G) (for instance an inner automorphism by an element of G) coincides with an automorphism of O^{x mu}(G) induced by an element of Gamma with nontrivial image in Z_p^x. Argument given: the composite of the cyclotomic character of G with the p-adic logarithm determines, by the definition of O^x(G) via abelianizations of open subgroups of G ([AbsTopIII] Proposition 5.8 (i)), a natural surjection O^{x mu}(G) -> Q_p ([AbsAnab] Proposition 1.2.1 (vi)) that is Aut(G)-equivariant for the trivial action of Aut(G) on Q_p and Gamma-equivariant for the natural action of Gamma in Zhat^x on Q_p through Zhat^x -> Z_p^x.
explicit_hypotheses: G a topological group isomorphic to G_k
Gamma a closed subgroup of Zhat^x as in Example 1.8 (iii)
implicit_hypotheses: O^{x mu}(G) as constructed in Example 1.8 (iv)
IUT2.Rem1_8_1.conclusion: An automorphism of O^{x mu}(G) induced by an element of Aut(G) never equals one induced by an element of Gamma whose image in Z_p^x is nontrivial.
obligations: No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.

The argument (page 42) rests on [AbsAnab] Proposition 1.2.1 (vi) (the Aut(G)-equivariance of the surjection to Q_p for the trivial action) and on the construction of [AbsTopIII] Proposition 5.8 (i). The deduction itself is short: an automorphism acting trivially on Q_p cannot equal one acting by a nontrivial element of Z_p^x, given that the surjection to Q_p is onto.
ambiguities: Page 42: the nontrivial element of Z_p^x acts on Q_p by multiplication; the conclusion needs that it acts nontrivially on the target Q_p, which holds since the map is surjective and Q_p is torsion-free. This step is left implicit.

IUT2.Ex1_9.content: Radial and coric data III: graphs of functorial group-theoretic algorithms. (i) The graph of a functor arising from a functorial algorithm; (ii) any functorial group-theoretic algorithm with input a topological group isomorphic to Pi^tp gives a multiradially defined functor, tautologically, via Example 1.8 (i); (iii) the same algorithm also gives a uniradially defined functor via a uniradial environment; (iv) application to the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l . Delta_Theta)(Pi) -> mu_Zhat(Pi/Delta), with three approaches (a), (b), (c).
obligations: Parent of the part records; the status of each part is given there.

IUT2.Ex1_9.i.content: (i) For categories E, F arising from types of mathematical data and a functor Xi: E -> F arising from a functorial algorithm (Example 1.7 (i)), the graph G of Xi is the category whose objects are pairs (E, Xi(E)), E in Ob(E), and whose morphisms are pairs (f: E -> E', Xi(f): Xi(E) -> Xi(E')); there are natural functors E -> G, G -> E, G -> F. This construction was used in the radial environments of Example 1.8.
explicit_hypotheses: E, F categories arising from types of mathematical data
Xi: E -> F a functor arising from a functorial algorithm
IUT2.Ex1_9.i.conclusion: Definition of the graph G of Xi and of the natural functors E -> G, G -> E, G -> F.
obligations: Definitional; the graph of a functor and the three functors are elementary category theory.

IUT2.Ex1_9.ii.content: (ii) Let E be the category of topological groups isomorphic to Pi^tp of X double underline_k and their isomorphisms, Xi a functorial group-theoretic algorithm with such input, and (R, C, Phi) the radial environment of Example 1.8 (i). Composing R -> E, (Pi, G, alpha) -> Pi, with Xi gives R -> F, whose graph is R^dagger; with the natural functors Psi_R: R -> R^dagger, R^dagger -> R -> C and C^dagger := C one obtains a diagram as in Example 1.7 (iv). Since (R, C, Phi) is multiradial, Psi_R is multiradially defined: any functorial group-theoretic algorithm with input a topological group isomorphic to Pi^tp gives rise, tautologically, to a multiradially defined functor.
explicit_hypotheses: Xi a functorial group-theoretic algorithm whose input is a topological group isomorphic to Pi^tp of X double underline_k
(R, C, Phi) the multiradial environment of Example 1.8 (i)
IUT2.Ex1_9.ii.conclusion: The functor Psi_R: R -> R^dagger built from Xi is multiradially defined.
obligations: The conclusion is immediate from the definition of multiradially defined (Example 1.7 (iv)), which depends only on the multiradiality of the source environment, established in Example 1.8 (i).

IUT2.Ex1_9.iii.content: (iii) Radial data: a topological group Pi isomorphic to Pi^tp, isomorphisms of topological groups; coric data and their isomorphisms as in Example 1.8 (i); radial functor Phi: R -> C, Pi -> Pi/Delta. Then Phi fails to be full ([AbsTopIII] Section I3, Remark 1.9.1), so (R, C, Phi) is uniradial. For Xi as in (ii), R is identified with E and the graph of Xi gives R^dagger with Psi_R: R -> R^dagger, Phi^dagger: R^dagger -> R -> C^dagger := C, a diagram as in Example 1.7 (iv); so Psi_R is uniradially defined: any functorial group-theoretic algorithm with input a topological group isomorphic to Pi^tp also gives rise, tautologically, to a uniradially defined functor.
explicit_hypotheses: Xi as in (ii)
IUT2.Ex1_9.iii.conclusion: The environment (Pi, Pi -> Pi/Delta) is uniradial, and the functor Psi_R built from Xi is uniradially defined.
obligations: No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.

Page 42 to 43: the failure of Pi -> Pi/Delta to be full (not every automorphism of Pi/Delta, as a topological group isomorphic to G_k, lifts to an automorphism of Pi) is asserted with a citation of [AbsTopIII] only.

IUT2.Ex1_9.iv.content: (iv) For Pi isomorphic to Pi^tp and Delta as in Example 1.8 (i), the inverse of the isomorphism mu_Zhat(G_k) -> mu_Zhat(Pi_X) of [AbsTopIII] Corollary 1.10 (c), constructed by a functorial group-theoretic algorithm, gives a cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l . Delta_Theta)(Pi) -> mu_Zhat(Pi/Delta) of Pi-modules ((l . Delta_Theta)(Pi) the subquotient of [EtTh] Corollary 2.18 (i); compare Proposition 1.3 (ii)). Taking this algorithm as Xi gives (a) a multiradially defined functor by (ii) and (b) a uniradially defined functor by (iii). (c) Alternatively, with (R, C, Phi) the multiradial environment of Example 1.8 (i), daggered radial data (Pi, G, alpha, (l . Delta_Theta)(Pi) -> mu_Zhat(G)) consist of (Pi, G, alpha) together with the poly-isomorphism obtained by composing the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism with the poly-isomorphism mu_Zhat(Pi/Delta) -> mu_Zhat(G) induced by alpha; it is a Gamma-orbit of isomorphisms of topological modules, Gamma in Zhat^x the image of Aut(G) by the cyclotomic character ([AbsAnab] Proposition 1.2.1 (vi)). Isomorphisms of daggered radial data are isomorphisms of the underlying radial data (necessarily compatible with the poly-isomorphism). With C^dagger := C this yields a functor Psi_R: R -> R^dagger arising from a functorial algorithm and a diagram as in Example 1.7 (iv); this multiradially defined functor is an alternative multiradial representation of the algorithm giving the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism, the approach of Corollary 1.11 (b).
explicit_hypotheses: Pi a topological group isomorphic to Pi^tp of X double underline_k; Delta in Pi as in Example 1.8 (i)
(R, C, Phi) the multiradial environment of Example 1.8 (i) (for (c))
IUT2.Ex1_9.iv.conclusion: The cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l . Delta_Theta)(Pi) -> mu_Zhat(Pi/Delta) gives (a) a multiradially defined functor, (b) a uniradially defined functor, and (c) a multiradially defined functor Psi_R: R -> R^dagger whose daggered radial data carry the cyclotomic rigidity only up to a Gamma-orbit.
obligations: No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.

The cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism comes from [AbsTopIII] Corollary 1.10 (c); that isomorphisms of daggered radial data are 'necessarily compatible' with the Gamma-orbit (page 44) is stated without argument.

IUT2.Rem1_9_1.content: The part of the algorithms of Example 1.9 (ii) to (iv) involving Pi/Delta depends not only on the abstract topological group Pi/Delta but on its structure as a quotient of Pi, i.e. on the arithmetic holomorphic structure. The multiradial terminology of Example 1.7 was introduced to compute which portions of the output of such algorithms depend essentially on the arithmetic holomorphic structure and which are mono-analytic, depending only on the topological group Pi/Delta. The tautological approach of Example 1.9 (ii) ((iv) (a)) corresponds to equipping each spoke Pi/Delta of Fig. 1.2 with a fixed arithmetic holomorphic structure related to the coric G only by an indeterminate isomorphism: a multiradially defined functor compatible with simultaneous execution on multiple spokes. The approach of Example 1.9 (iii) ((iv) (b)) identifies the spokes via arbitrary mono-analytic isomorphisms: a uniradially defined functor that can be executed consistently on one spoke at a time. The approach of Example 1.9 (iv) (c) weakens the rigidity of the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism to a specified indeterminacy and obtains a multiradially defined functor compatible with gluing isomorphisms; its multiradiality depends essentially on the content of the algorithm. This is representative of Corollaries 1.10, 1.11 and 1.12, which may be regarded as computations of the indeterminacy needed.
IUT2.Rem1_9_1.conclusion: Of the three approaches of Example 1.9 (iv), (a) is tautologically multiradial, (b) is uniradial (one spoke at a time), and (c) is multiradial up to a specified indeterminacy, the model for Corollaries 1.10 to 1.12.
obligations: Interpretive commentary on Example 1.9; the formal content is that of Example 1.9 (ii) to (iv).

IUT2.Rem1_9_2.content: (i) Uniradially defined functors correspond to constructions depending strictly on the arithmetic holomorphic structure, corically defined ones to constructions depending only on the mono-analytic (arithmetic real analytic) structure, and multiradially defined ones to constructions depending on the arithmetic holomorphic structure only in a way compatible with a given description of how it is related to (embedded in) the mono-analytic structure; in Example 1.8 this description is given by the poly-morphisms alpha_(-) of the radial data (summarized in Fig. 1.3, comparing with holomorphic and real analytic structures in classical complex Teichmuller theory). (ii) With the analogy of Remark 1.7.1, a multiradial environment allows parallel transport between distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures related only via the mono-analytic core. (iii) The approaches of Example 1.9 (iv) (a), (c) are analogous to distinct connection structures on one fibration; the tautological approach (a), comparable to the tautological construction of connections in the p-adic crystalline theory via the PD-envelope of the diagonal, works with labels of all possible arithmetic holomorphic structures (choices of one arrow of the poly-morphism alpha of Example 1.8 (i)) and is less interesting than the non-tautological approach (c), which explicitly computes indeterminacies and so describes structures attached to an alien arithmetic holomorphic structure.
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Examples 1.7 to 1.9 and Remarks 1.7.1, 1.9.1
IUT2.Rem1_9_2.conclusion: Uniradial, multiradial and corically defined functors correspond to dependence on the arithmetic holomorphic structure, dependence compatible with its relation to the mono-analytic structure, and dependence on the mono-analytic structure only (Fig. 1.3); the non-tautological approach of Example 1.9 (iv) (c) is preferred because it computes indeterminacies explicitly.
obligations: Interpretive commentary with analogies (connections, crystalline site, complex Teichmuller theory); no mathematical assertion beyond the definitions of Example 1.7.
ambiguities: Page 45: 'stuctures' in part (ii) is a misprint for 'structures'.

IUT2.Rem1_10_1.content: The domain and codomain of the isomorphism (*^{mono-Theta}_Pi) of Corollary 1.10, and the isomorphism itself, are built from subquotients of the projective system of topological groups Delta_{M^Theta_*(Pi)} determined by: the structure of Delta_{M^Theta_*(Pi)} as a projective system of topological groups; the subgroups given by the images of the theta section portions of the mono-theta environments M^Theta_*(Pi); and the images of (l . Z)(M^Theta_*(Pi)) and G(M^Theta_*(Pi)) in Out(Delta_{M^Theta_*(Pi)}) (Definition 1.1 (i)). The algorithms in the proofs of [EtTh] Corollaries 2.18 (i), (iii) and 2.19 (i) for these subquotients and for the graph of the isomorphism depend only on the projective system Delta_{M^Theta_*(Pi)} ([EtTh] Proposition 2.11 (i)), on these theta section images ([EtTh] Definition 2.13 (ii), (c)), and on the construction of Delta_C(Pi) (Proposition 1.6 (i)) containing Delta_Y(M^Theta_*(Pi)) in Delta_X(M^Theta_*(Pi)) (Y, X double underline), isomorphic to Delta, used for the subquotients of [EtTh] Propositions 2.12, 2.14 (i).
IUT2.Rem1_10_1.conclusion: The isomorphism (*^{mono-Theta}_Pi), its domain and its codomain depend only on the projective system Delta_{M^Theta_*(Pi)}, the images of the theta section portions, the images of (l . Z)(M^Theta_*(Pi)) and G(M^Theta_*(Pi)) in Out(Delta_{M^Theta_*(Pi)}), and Delta_C(Pi).
obligations: No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.
Page 47: the dependence claim is justified by pointing to the algorithms in the proofs of [EtTh] Corollaries 2.18 and 2.19; a formalization depends on them.

IUT2.Rem1_10_3.content: Recalls ([EtTh] Remark 1.10.4 (ii)) that it is by no means clear that a more general meromorphic function than the theta function satisfies the cyclotomic, discrete and constant multiple rigidity properties of [EtTh]. Cyclotomic rigidity, the basis of Corollary 1.10, depends most explicitly ([EtTh] Remark 2.19.2) on the theta quotient 1 -> Delta_Theta -> Delta^Theta_X -> Delta^ell_X -> 1 ([IUTchI] Remark 3.1.2 (iii)), corresponding to the theta group of classical treatments; since the theta function is essentially characterized among meromorphic functions by the theta symmetries arising from the theta group, it is difficult to see how to generalize the theory to more general meromorphic functions (Remark 1.1.1 (v); [IUTchIII] Remark 2.3.3). Unlike the theta function, which is local (defined a priori at v in V^bad), the theta quotient Delta^Theta_X, hence Delta_Theta, is defined globally over the number fields involved ([IUTchI] Remark 3.1.2), so it can be used in global anabelian reconstruction via the Theta-approach.
IUT2.Rem1_10_3.conclusion: Cyclotomic rigidity depends explicitly on the theta quotient; generalizing the theory beyond the theta function is not evident; the theta quotient and Delta_Theta are defined globally, unlike the theta function.
definitions_required: theta quotient 1 -> Delta_Theta -> Delta^Theta_X -> Delta^ell_X -> 1 ([IUTchI] Remark 3.1.2 (iii))
obligations: Commentary; the statements that more general meromorphic functions need not satisfy the rigidity properties and that the theta function is essentially characterized by the theta symmetries are heuristic ('roughly speaking') and are not claimed as theorems.

IUT2.Rem1_11_1.content: (i) Recalls, for G isomorphic to G_k: (a) the automorphism group of the MLF-Galois TM-pair G acting on O^triangleright(G) ([AbsTopIII] Definition 3.1 (ii)) maps bijectively, by forgetting O^triangleright(G), onto Aut(G) ([AbsTopIII] Proposition 3.2 (iv)); (b) the automorphism group of the MLF-Galois TCG-pair G acting on O^x(G) maps surjectively onto Aut(G), with kernel the G-linear automorphisms of O^x(G) given by the natural action of Zhat^x ([AbsTopIII] Proposition 3.3 (ii)); (c) by the same Kummer-map proof as for (b), the automorphism group of G acting on O^gp-hat(G) (ind-topological module with group action) maps surjectively onto Aut(G) with kernel given by the natural action of Zhat^x, equivalently maps bijectively onto the automorphism group of G acting on O^x(G); (d) the underlying ind-topological module of O^{x mu}(G) is divisible, hence has a natural Q_p-action; so replacing O^x by O^{x mu} in (b) makes the description of the kernel false. (ii) The case of interest of Corollary 1.11 is Gamma = Zhat^x: a Zhat^x-multiple indeterminacy corresponds exactly to working with the underlying ind-topological module with group action of G acting on O^x(G) (by (i) (b)).
explicit_hypotheses: G a topological group isomorphic to G_k
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Corollary 1.11 and Example 1.8
IUT2.Rem1_11_1.conclusion: (a) Aut(G on O^triangleright(G)) = Aut(G); (b) Aut(G on O^x(G)) -> Aut(G) is surjective with kernel Zhat^x; (c) the same for O^gp-hat(G); (d) O^{x mu}(G) is divisible with a Q_p-action, so (b) fails for O^{x mu}; (ii) Corollary 1.11 is used with Gamma = Zhat^x.
obligations: No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.

(a), (b) are cited from [AbsTopIII] Propositions 3.2 (iv), 3.3 (ii). (c) is asserted 'by the same proof' as [AbsTopIII] Proposition 3.3 (ii), not written out (page 50). (d) is said to be verified 'immediately' (page 50); the divisibility of O^{x mu}(G) and the falsity of the kernel description for O^{x mu} are given without argument.

IUT2.Rem1_11_2.content: (i) The natural action of Zhat^x on G acting on O^x(G) (Remark 1.11.1 (i) (b)) is compatible with pull-back along Pi -> Pi/Delta composed with any isomorphism Pi/Delta -> G (Example 1.8), so Zhat^x acts naturally on the pair Pi acting on O^x(G). This action fails to be compatible with the ring structure on O^x(G) tensor Q (determined by the p-adic logarithm): although the ring structure on O^x can be reconstructed from Pi ([AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9), unlike from G, the natural Zhat^x-action on Pi acting on O^x(G) does not preserve it. (ii) This explains the use of G rather than Pi in the Theta-link between distinct Theta-Hodge theaters ([IUTchI] Corollary 3.7): working with Pi acting on O^x(G) does not give a consistent common arithmetic holomorphic structure, since distinct Theta-Hodge theaters share only a common O^x ([IUTchI] Corollary 3.7 (iii)), on which Zhat^x acts, not a common O^triangleright; a common O^triangleright is obstructed essentially by the valuative portion Theta_v -> q_v of the Theta-link ([IUTchI] Remark 3.8.1 (i)).
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Example 1.8 and Remark 1.11.1
IUT2.Rem1_11_2.conclusion: Zhat^x acts on Pi acting on O^x(G) but does not preserve the ring structure on O^x(G) tensor Q reconstructed from Pi; hence using Pi instead of G in the Theta-link would not yield a common arithmetic holomorphic structure across Theta-Hodge theaters.
definitions_required: ring structure on O^x tensor Q via the p-adic logarithm
obligations: Page 51: the failure of the Zhat^x-action to preserve the ring structure on O^x(G) tensor Q is stated without argument.
ambiguities: Page 51: the double underlines on Theta_v and q_v in the valuative portion are read on the 100 dpi render; the page refers to [IUTchI] Remark 3.8.1 (i) for the meaning.

IUT2.Rem1_11_3.content: Commentary on the coric data and indeterminacies of Corollaries 1.10 and 1.11, in five parts: (i) specification of coric data and forgetting anabelian structures; (ii) gluing G acting on O^{x mu}(G) across Theta-Hodge theaters up to an (Aut(G), Zhat^x)-indeterminacy; (iii) post-anabelian input data and the source of the indeterminacies; (iv) elimination of the indeterminacy by uniradial functors; (v) why post-anabelian input matters.
obligations: Parent of the part records; the status of each part is given there.

IUT2.Rem1_11_3.i.content: (i) A discussion of radial environments starts from the radial functor, i.e. which portion of the radial data is taken as coric data. From [IUTchI] Section 3 (especially at v in V^bad, Corollaries 3.7, 3.9) the coric data should include the quotient Pi -> Pi/Delta, isomorphic to G, of Pi in a Theta-Hodge theater. In [IUTchIII] the theory of [AbsTopIII] Sections 3, 5 is applied, where objects (Pi acting on M_TM(Pi), G acting on O^triangleright(G), G acting on O^x(G)) are constructed group-theoretically and then their anabelian structure is forgotten. Objects built from G with their anabelian structure are naturally part of the coric data; once it is forgotten, it must be specified explicitly that such an object belongs to the coric data, i.e. is subject to the gluing of Example 1.7 (v).
IUT2.Rem1_11_3.i.conclusion: Objects constructed from G are coric only while their anabelian structure is retained; after forgetting it, coricity must be specified explicitly.
obligations: Methodological commentary on the choice of coric data; no assertion to formalize beyond the definitions of Example 1.7.

IUT2.Rem1_11_3.ii.content: (ii) By the coricity of O^x ([IUTchI] Corollary 3.7 (iii)) one may take the underlying MLF-Galois TCG-pair G acting on O^x(G) as coric data; by Remark 1.11.1 (i) (b) this means working with it up to an (Aut(G), Gamma = Zhat^x)-indeterminacy, the p-adic portion of the Gamma-indeterminacy not being subsumed in the Aut(G)-indeterminacy (Remark 1.8.1); this is the situation of Example 1.8 (iii). To construct the multiradially defined functors of Corollaries 1.10, 1.12, one passes to O^{x mu}(-) = O^x(-)/O^mu(-), but not solely to the module G acting on O^{x mu}(G) (Example 1.8 (ix), Remark 1.11.1 (i) (d)). By [IUTchI] Corollary 3.7 (iii) and Remark 1.11.1 (i) (b), one can glue consistently the G acting on O^{x mu}(G) (Fig. 1.4) from distinct Theta-Hodge theaters up to an (Aut(G), Zhat^x)-indeterminacy, as formulated in Example 1.8 (v), (vi), (viii), (ix) with Gamma^{x mu} = Im(Gamma). Even with G acting on O^{x mu}(G) as coric data, compatibility with the natural maps O^gp-hat(G) <- O^x(G) -> O^{x mu}(G) (Example 1.8 (viii)) implies that the (Aut(G), Zhat^x)-indeterminacy on G acting on O^{x mu}(G) induces one on G acting on O^x(G) and on O^gp-hat(G), the latter representing the Gamma-indeterminacy in specifying O^triangleright(G) in O^gp-hat(G); these induce the orbits of Corollary 1.11 (a), (b), in contrast with the strict cyclotomic rigidity of Corollary 1.10 (Remark 1.10.2).
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Corollaries 1.10, 1.11 and Example 1.8
IUT2.Rem1_11_3.ii.conclusion: The G acting on O^{x mu}(G) from distinct Theta-Hodge theaters can be glued consistently up to an (Aut(G), Zhat^x)-indeterminacy, and this indeterminacy induces (Aut(G), Zhat^x)-indeterminacies on G acting on O^x(G) and O^gp-hat(G), which are the orbits of Corollary 1.11 (a), (b).
obligations: Page 52: the consistent gluing is concluded from [IUTchI] Corollary 3.7 (iii) and Remark 1.11.1 (i) (b) without a written argument; the claim that compatibility with O^gp-hat(G) <- O^x(G) -> O^{x mu}(G) 'implies' the induced indeterminacies is stated without derivation. A formalization would need the precise statement of how the indeterminacy on the quotient O^{x mu} induces one on O^x and O^gp-hat.

IUT2.Rem1_11_3.iii.content: (iii) The cyclotomic rigidity algorithms of Corollaries 1.10 and 1.11 (a) compose a group-theoretic construction with an algorithm whose input is post-anabelian (obtained after forgetting the anabelian structure): a system of mono-theta environments for Corollary 1.10, an MLF-Galois TM-pair for Corollary 1.11 (a). The indeterminacies acting on this input induce the orbits of Corollary 1.11 (a), (b). (a) These orbits come from the nontrivial relation between the input O^triangleright(-) and the coric data O^{x mu}(-). (b) The strict cyclotomic rigidity of Corollary 1.10 comes from the triviality of the homomorphism relating the cyclotomic portion of O^triangleright(-), the only portion appearing in a mono-theta environment, to the coric data O^{x mu}(-) (Remark 1.10.2). This shows that not only the existence but also the content of a reconstruction algorithm matters ([IUTchIV] Example 3.5).
IUT2.Rem1_11_3.iii.conclusion: The orbits of Corollary 1.11 (a), (b) arise from the nontrivial relation of O^triangleright(-) to O^{x mu}(-); the strict cyclotomic rigidity of Corollary 1.10 arises from the triviality of the map from the cyclotomic portion to O^{x mu}(-).
obligations: Commentary explaining the source of the indeterminacies; the triviality in (b) is that of Remark 1.10.2, already recorded there.

IUT2.Rem1_11_3.iv.content: (iv) The (Aut(G), Gamma)-indeterminacy of Corollary 1.11 (a), (b) can be eliminated by working, as in Example 1.9 (iv) (b), with uniradially defined functors: replace G acting on O^triangleright(G) by Pi acting on M_TM(Pi) and G by Pi/Delta, and use the uniradial environment (Pi acting on M_TM(Pi)) -> (Pi/Delta acting on M^{x mu}_TM(Pi)), whose coric data coincide with those of the multiradial environment of Corollary 1.11.
IUT2.Rem1_11_3.iv.conclusion: With the uniradial environment (Pi acting on M_TM(Pi)) -> (Pi/Delta acting on M^{x mu}_TM(Pi)) the indeterminacy of Corollary 1.11 (a), (b) disappears, at the cost of uniradiality.
obligations: Page 53: the elimination of the indeterminacy is stated in passing and not proved; a formalization would need to define this uniradial environment and check that its output carries no indeterminacy.

IUT2.Rem1_11_3.v.content: (v) Post-anabelian input is wanted so that the same algorithms apply to input not arising from a group-theoretic construction, e.g. the divisor and rational function monoid portion of a Frobenioid as in Proposition 1.3. There the exterior cyclotome of the mono-theta environment of Corollary 1.10 and the cyclotome from O^triangleright(-) of Corollary 1.11 (a) both correspond to the same cyclotome mu_N(S) of the Frobenioid. At the level of construction algorithms, relating Pi_mu(M^Theta_*(Pi)) of Corollary 1.10 to mu_Zhat(O^x(G)) of Corollary 1.11 (a) requires (Proposition 1.3 (iii)) passing through (l . Delta_Theta)(Pi) via the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms of Corollaries 1.10 and 1.11, which for 1.11 introduces indeterminacies. So the Frobenioid-theoretic identification via mu_N(S) of these cyclotomes is either only uniradially defined (iv), or multiradially defined only up to indeterminacies.
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Proposition 1.3 and Corollaries 1.10, 1.11
IUT2.Rem1_11_3.v.conclusion: The Frobenioid-theoretic identification of Pi_mu(M^Theta_*(Pi)) and mu_Zhat(O^x(G)) via mu_N(S) is uniradially defined, or multiradially defined only up to indeterminacies.
obligations: Page 54: that the Frobenioid-theoretic identification is multiradially defined only up to indeterminacies is asserted from the structure of the algorithms, without proof.

IUT2.Rem1_11_4.content: (i) The cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism of Corollary 1.10, i.e. the triviality of the homomorphism relating the cyclotomic portion of O^triangleright(-) to the coric data O^{x mu}(-) (Remark 1.11.3 (iii) (b)), compared with Corollary 1.11 (with indeterminacies from the nontrivial relation of O^triangleright(-) to O^{x mu}(-), Remark 1.11.3 (iii) (a)), may be seen as a splitting or decoupling that separates the purely radial data of the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism of Corollary 1.10 from the purely coric data O^{x mu}(-) (Remark 1.12.2 (vi)). (ii) In the language of Remark 1.9.2 (iii), the purely radial data depend on the tautological collection of labels of all possible arithmetic holomorphic structures; the algorithms of Corollary 1.10 do not describe these labels explicitly in terms of O^{x mu}(-). A modified version (*) of Corollary 1.10 replaces O^{x mu}(-) by O^x(-) (so the triviality of Remark 1.11.3 (iii) (b) fails) and uses the tautological approach of Example 1.9 (iv) (a), without indeterminacies; then the codomain becomes the submodule O^mu(-) of the purely coric data O^x(-), with a rigidity depending on the choice of label. Corollary 1.10 as stated is not free of label-dependence, but confines it to the purely radial component, yielding a purely coric component free of label-dependent data: its output splits into label-dependent (purely radial) and label-independent (purely coric) components.
IUT2.Rem1_11_4.conclusion: The output of Corollary 1.10 decouples into a label-dependent purely radial component and a label-independent purely coric component O^{x mu}(-), unlike the modified version (*) with O^x(-), whose cyclotome O^mu(-) inside the coric data carries label-dependent rigidity.
obligations: Interpretive commentary; the formal content (triviality of Pi_mu tensor Q/Z -> O^{x mu}(G)) is that of Remark 1.10.2 and Corollary 1.10.
ambiguities: The index gives pages 54 to 55; the render of page 55 shows Remark 1.11.5 at its top, so Remark 1.11.4 ends on page 54.

IUT2.Rem1_12_4.content: The theta evaluation algorithm of Corollary 1.12 (ii), by restriction to the decomposition groups of the point mu_-, uses only the topological group Pi as input; this is crucial when the theory is combined with log-shells ([AbsTopIII]) in [IUTchIII]. Given some evaluation algorithm (abstract theta function) -> (theta values), not necessarily restriction to the decomposition group of a closed point, it is natural ([EtTh] Remark 1.10.4; the log-wall of [AbsTopIII] Section I4; Remark 1.12.3) to require compatibility with forming Kummer classes by extracting N-th roots of the abstract theta function and of the theta values, hence extension to coverings (e.g. Galois coverings) of input and output; functoriality for the Galois groups on both sides (Fig. 1.5) then leads to the principle of Galois evaluation: the evaluation algorithm arises from a section G -> Pi_{Y-double-dot}(Pi) of the natural surjection Pi_{Y-double-dot}(Pi) -> G. By the Section Conjecture of anabelian geometry one expects such continuous sections to arise from geometric points (compare [IUTchI] Example 4.5 (i), Remark 2.5.1). Group-theoreticity of the evaluation algorithm is an abstract analogue of compatibility with Frobenius crystal structures in p-adic theory ([AbsTopIII] Section I5).
IUT2.Rem1_12_4.conclusion: Requiring an evaluation algorithm to be compatible with Kummer classes and functorial with respect to Galois groups forces, in effect, that it arise from a section G -> Pi_{Y-double-dot}(Pi) of Pi_{Y-double-dot}(Pi) -> G (principle of Galois evaluation); by the Section Conjecture such sections are expected to come from geometric points.
obligations: Page 61: the passage from 'natural requirements' (Kummer compatibility, extension to coverings, Galois functoriality) to the conclusion that the evaluation arises from a section is described as leading 'in effect' to that conclusion; the requirements are not made precise and no argument is given. The Section Conjecture is an open conjecture and is invoked only as an expectation.

IUT2.Rem1_12_5.content: Analogy with the Gaussian integral, in three parts. (i) Scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory ([HASurI], [HASurII]) is a scheme-theoretic version of the computation of the Gaussian integral, integral over R of e^{-x^2} dx = sqrt(pi), via the square of the integral over R^2 in polar coordinates: its comparison isomorphism ([HASurI] Theorem A) between a de Rham side (sections of an ample line bundle on the universal extension of an elliptic curve, with Hodge filtration) and an etale side (functions on the l-torsion points, with GL_2(F_l)-action) parallels cartesian versus polar coordinates (Fig. 1.6); e^{-x^2} appears in the Gaussian poles of the de Rham side ([HASurI] Section 1.1); sqrt(pi) corresponds to negative tensor powers of the sheaf omega, via the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism between omega^{tensor 2} and the restriction of the log differentials of the moduli stack ([HASurII] Theorems 2.8, 2.10); the relation is explicit at archimedean primes via the Hermite model. (ii) Inter-universal Teichmuller theory may be thought of as a global arithmetic/Galois-theoretic version of the Gaussian integral: the step-like cartesian representation resembles the Frobenius-picture ([IUTchI] Corollary 3.8, Remark 3.8.1), the rotational symmetry of polar coordinates resembles the etale-picture ([IUTchI] Corollary 3.9); the etale-picture of the multiradial functor of Corollary 1.12 (Fig. 1.7: copies of infinity-theta(Pi) on spokes around the mono-analytic core G acting on O^{x mu}(G) acted on by Ism), from the series sum over n in Z of q^{n^2} U^n ([EtTh] Proposition 1.4), resembles the polar representation; the change of variables e^{-r^2} to u in 2 (integral e^{-x^2} dx)^2 = 2 double integral e^{-x^2-y^2} dx dy = double integral e^{-r^2} 2r dr dtheta = double integral d(e^{-r^2}) dtheta = double integral du dtheta is formally reminiscent of the Theta-link Theta_v -> q_v ([IUTchI] Remark 3.8.1 (i)). (iii) As the equivalence of cartesian and polar representations is used to compute the Gaussian integral, the relation between Frobenius- and etale-pictures plays a central role ([IUTchIII] Section 3; [IUTchIV] Section 1).
IUT2.Rem1_12_5.conclusion: Analogies: Hodge-Arakelov theory and inter-universal Teichmuller theory are compared with the polar-coordinate computation of the Gaussian integral; Frobenius-picture versus etale-picture corresponds to cartesian versus polar coordinates, and the Theta-link to the substitution u = e^{-r^2}.
obligations: Analogy only; no mathematical claim about IUT objects. The classical identity integral over R of e^{-x^2} dx = sqrt(pi) is a standard result (available in Mathlib as the Gaussian integral).
ambiguities: Page 63: in the displayed chain, double integral e^{-r^2} 2r dr dtheta = double integral d(e^{-r^2}) dtheta holds only up to sign, since d(e^{-r^2}) = -2r e^{-r^2} dr; the integration limits are not written, so the sign is absorbed by orientation. The page calls the analogy 'formal'.
The index gives pages 61 to 64; the render of page 64 shows Section 2 starting at its top, so the remark ends on page 63.

IUT2.Rem3_6_3.content: Observations on basepoints for the non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters of Remark 3.6.2. (i) In the theory of etale fundamental groups the fiber functor of a basepoint is defined by points of a finite etale covering, valued in a separably closed field, over a fixed point of the base; over the spectrum of a field these are ring homomorphisms into a separably closed field, so the scheme-theoretic notion of basepoint depends essentially on ring/scheme structure. Consequently the distinct ring structures on either side of a non-ring/scheme-theoretic filter (the log-wall of [AbsTopIII], the Theta-link of [IUTchI] Corollary 3.7) give rise to distinct, unrelated basepoints ([AbsTopIII] Remark 3.7.7 (i)). (ii) The same applies to N-th power morphisms (N > 1), the morphisms of Frobenius type of Frobenioids: in the tempered Frobenioids of [EtTh] Section 5 they induce N-th power morphisms between monoids isomorphic to O^triangleright_{K_v}, which fail to preserve the ring structure of K_v and so give distinct, unrelated basepoints on domain and codomain. Unlike (i), these take place compatibly with the projection functor to the base category of the Frobenioid, so the unrelated basepoints only give rise to inner automorphisms of the topological group determined by the base category; N-th power morphisms are milder, algebraic operations that fit into a single category (the tempered Frobenioid, definable via formal flat O_{K_v}-schemes, [EtTh] Section 1), whereas the log-wall and Theta-link are drastic, non-algebraic, and difficult to fit into a single category lying over the same base category (Remark 1.11.2 (ii); [AbsTopIII] Remark 3.7.7). The study of the structures generated by the log-wall and Theta-link is a main theme of the series ([IUTchIII]).
IUT2.Rem3_6_3.conclusion: The log-wall and the Theta-link, being incompatible with ring structures, give distinct, unrelated basepoints on either side; N-th power morphisms of Frobenioids also give unrelated basepoints, but only up to inner automorphisms of the base group, because they are compatible with the projection to the base category.
definitions_required: morphism of Frobenius type (N-th power morphism) of a Frobenioid
obligations: Page 105: the claim that the unrelated basepoints of N-th power morphisms give only inner automorphisms of the base group is stated as a consequence of compatibility with the projection functor without a written argument. The rest is commentary on the scheme-theoretic definition of basepoints.

IUT2.Rem3_6_5.content: Philosophical observations on mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity. (i) A cyclotome is a kind of skeleton of the arithmetic holomorphic structure (Remark 1.11.6), motivated by the circle S^1 as skeleton of C^x at archimedean primes. (ii) The commutator structure [-,-] of the theta group (a) is central to mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity ([EtTh] Introduction, Remark 2.19.2) and (b) in the classical theory of algebraic theta functions implies irreducibility of certain representations of the theta group; both are instances of (c): the commutator structure embodies the coherence of holomorphic structures. In Hodge-Arakelov theory ([HASurI], [HASurII]) the irreducible representations among functions on l-torsion points are, for large l, discrete analogues of holomorphic functions among real analytic ones; conjugate synchronization (Remarks 3.5.2, 3.8.3), using the connected subgraph Gamma^triangle of Gamma_X (Remark 2.6.1 (i)), is a discretely parametrized coherence of arithmetic holomorphic structures, and mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity a continuously parametrized version supported on Y-double-dot_v; their interaction via restriction is central in the Galois evaluation of Corollaries 2.8 (i), 3.5 (ii), 3.6 (ii). (iii) With cyclotomes at localizations as local skeleta, mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity is a local uniformization of the number field (exterior cyclotome of Proposition 1.3 (i)) via a local portion (interior cyclotome) of the geometric tempered fundamental group Delta_v of a covering of X_F (Definition 2.3 (i); [IUTchI] Definition 3.1 (e)); it says the theta function from a mono-theta environment is free of Zhat^x-power indeterminacies, and constant multiple rigidity says the local uniformization is free of constant multiple indeterminacies. Analogies with p-adic Teichmuller theory ([AbsTopIII] Section I5, [pTeich] Section 0.9): X_F corresponds to nilpotent ordinary indigenous bundles, local uniformizations to canonical coordinates, cyclotomic rigidity to the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism, Theta-links of the Frobenius-picture to transitions mod p^n to mod p^{n+1} of Witt vectors ([IUTchI] Section I4; [IUTchIII] Remark 1.4.1 (iii)), the multiradiality of Corollary 1.12 to the Frobenius invariance of canonical coordinates, and discrete rigidity of [EtTh] to canonical coordinates being power series rather than PD-formal power series; without discrete rigidity one would need Zhat-powers of U and q ([EtTh] Remarks 1.6.4, 2.19.4), analogous to O-hat-powers of canonical parameters requiring PD-formal power series ([pOrd] Chapter III).
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Remark 3.6.4 and Section 1
IUT2.Rem3_6_5.conclusion: Mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity is interpreted as a continuously parametrized coherence of arithmetic holomorphic structures and as a local uniformization free of Zhat^x-power indeterminacies; constant multiple rigidity as freedom from constant multiple indeterminacies; discrete rigidity as analogous to canonical coordinates being genuine power series.
definitions_required: theta group and its commutator structure
obligations: Philosophical commentary with analogies; the mathematical statements it interprets (cyclotomic, constant multiple and discrete rigidity) are those of [EtTh] and of Corollaries 1.10, 1.12.
ambiguities: Page 109: 'That it to say' is a misprint for 'That is to say'.
Page 109: the subgraph is printed as Gamma with a filled triangle superscript and X double underline subscript, read on the 100 dpi render; Remark 2.6.1 (i) defines it.

IUT2.Rem3_8_3.content: What Section 3 gains from the conjugate synchronization of Section 2 (Remark 3.5.2), in three parts. (i) Direct technical consequences: (a) the isomorphisms of monoids Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{|t1|} -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{|t2|}, (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{|t1|} -> (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{|t2|}, (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{|t|} -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{|t|}, for |t|, |t1|, |t2| in |F_l|, the third well defined up to an inner automorphism indeterminacy independent of |t| (Corollaries 3.5 (i), 3.6 (i)); (b) the well-defined diagonal submonoids Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{<|F_l|>} in the product over |t| in |F_l| and Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{<F_l^*>} in the product over |t| in F_l^* (Corollary 3.5 (i)), and the diagonal embeddings of categories (constant distributions) of Definition 3.8 (iii); (c) the well-defined isomorphisms Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_0 -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{<F_l^*>} and (Psi_{dagger C_v})_0 -> (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{<F_l^*>} (Corollaries 3.5 (iii), 3.6 (iii)); (d) the restriction to units of the composite isomorphism Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v, alpha} -> Psi_{F_xi}(dagger F_v) of the third display of Corollary 3.6 (ii). (b), (c) are formal consequences of (a), and (d) is an alternate formulation of the units part of (a) for |t| in F_l^*. The main application (Section 4) of conjugate synchronization is the isomorphism of units of (d), composed with the Theta-link (coricity of O^x, [IUTchI] Corollary 3.7 (iii)); the isomorphisms of monoids in the Theta-link or in Corollary 3.6 (ii) make sense only for post-anabelian abstract monoids/Frobenioids (Frobenius-like structures). (ii) In [IUTchIII], etale-like versions of the Frobenioid-theoretic theta and Gaussian monoids able to penetrate the log-wall are constructed via Kummer theory, which uses the cyclotomes in the unit groups; this needs conjugate synchronization in an essential way: without it, by the unrelated basepoints on either side of the log-wall (Remark 3.6.3 (i)), one could only form diagonal embeddings of submonoids of Galois invariants or of sets of Galois orbits of the constant monoids Psi_cns, which are insufficient for Kummer theory ([IUTchIII] Remark 1.5.1 (ii)), and passing to Galois orbits is incompatible with the ring (additive) structure of the constant monoids (with {0} adjoined), which the log-wall requires within each Hodge theater (Remark 3.6.4 (i)). (iii) Conjugate synchronization and mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity (Remark 3.6.5 (ii)) are instances of the theme of explicitly describing one arithmetic holomorphic structure from another related only by a mono-analytic core; classically the natural isomorphisms between cyclotomes are taken for granted, with no explicit intrinsic reconstruction algorithms.
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Corollaries 3.5, 3.6 and Definition 3.8
IUT2.Rem3_8_3.conclusion: Conjugate synchronization yields the isomorphisms (a) to (d), of which (b), (c) are formal consequences of (a) and (d) is a reformulation of the units part of (a); its main use is the isomorphism of units (d) composed with the Theta-link, and it is essential for the Kummer theory needed to pass the log-wall, since Galois invariants or orbits are insufficient and incompatible with ring structure.
obligations: Page 117: that (b), (c) are formal consequences of (a) and (d) an alternate formulation of part of (a) is stated without derivation. Page 118: the insufficiency of Galois invariants or orbits for Kummer theory is called clear, and the incompatibility of Galois orbits with the additive structure is asserted without argument.
ambiguities: The index gives pages 117 to 120; the remark ends at the top of page 119 (rest of the page blank) and Section 4 starts on page 120.

IUT2.Rem4_1_1.content: (i) Proposition 4.1 is an easy formal generalization of the portion of Sections 2, 3 formed by Proposition 3.1 and Corollaries 2.4, 3.5 to v in V^good intersect V^non; compared with Sections 2, 3 it is somewhat tautological and for the most part vacuous; its purpose is to globalize the theory by gluing the theories at v in V^bad and v in V^good. (ii) The symmetrizing isomorphisms of Proposition 4.1 (iii) are the analogue at good nonarchimedean v of the conjugate synchronization at bad v (Corollary 3.5 (i), Remark 3.5.2); the copies of G_v(Pi_v) labeled by t in LabCusp^{+-}(Pi_v) are naturally the quotients D_t/I_t, where I_t in Pi_v is a cuspidal inertia group corresponding to t and D_t its decomposition group (the normalizer, equivalently the commensurator, of I_t in Pi_v; [AbsSect] Theorem 1.3 (ii)), with the isomorphism D_t/I_t -> G_v(Pi_v) induced by Pi_v -> G_v(Pi_v). (iii) There is an easy tautological formal analogue at good nonarchimedean v of the multiradiality and uniradiality assertions of Proposition 3.4 and Corollary 3.7: (a) the construction of Psi_cns(Pi_v) (Proposition 4.1 (i)) is uniradial (compare Proposition 3.4 (ii)); (b) the constructions of Psi^ss_cns(Pi_v), Psi_env(Pi_v), Psi_gau(Pi_v) (Proposition 4.1 (ii), (iv)) and of the isomorphism Psi_env(Pi_v) -> Psi_gau(Pi_v) are multiradial. The details are left to the reader. Ultimately ([IUTchIII]) a global analogue of the multiradiality and uniradiality of Sections 1, 3 is wanted, specializing to Sections 1, 3 at bad v and to (a), (b) at good nonarchimedean v.
explicit_hypotheses: v in V^good intersect V^non (for (ii), (iii))
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Proposition 4.1: initial Theta-data as in [IUTchI] Definition 3.1
IUT2.Rem4_1_1.conclusion: At good nonarchimedean v: Proposition 4.1 formally generalizes Proposition 3.1 and Corollaries 2.4, 3.5; the labeled copies of G_v(Pi_v) are D_t/I_t; the construction of Psi_cns(Pi_v) is uniradial, and those of Psi^ss_cns(Pi_v), Psi_env(Pi_v), Psi_gau(Pi_v) and of Psi_env(Pi_v) -> Psi_gau(Pi_v) are multiradial.
obligations: No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.

With Psi_cns(Pi_v) := Psi_cns(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)) (Proposition 3.1 (ii)), the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms of Definition 1.1 (ii) and the beginning of Corollary 2.9 give a functorial group-theoretic Pi_v-equivariant isomorphism Psi_cns(Pi_v)^x -> Psi^ss_cns(G_v(Pi_v))^x; there are analogues of Psi^ss_{dagger F^vdash_v} and of Proposition 4.2 (i), (ii) at bad v (details left to the reader). IUT2.Rem4_5_1.content: (i) As in Definition 3.8, the collections of monoids of Corollary 4.5 (i), (iv) may be interpreted as collections of Frobenioids: those of Corollary 4.5 (i) give an F-prime-strip, hence an F^vdash-prime-strip; the theta and Gaussian monoids of Corollary 4.5 (iv) give a well-defined F^vdash-prime-strip up to an indeterminacy at v in V^bad (corresponding to the 2l-th roots of the square of the theta function and to the value-profiles) relative to automorphisms of the split Frobenioid at such v inducing the identity on the subcategory of isometries ([FrdI] Theorem 5.1 (iii)) of the underlying category (Remark 4.10.1). As in Remark 3.8.1, this Frobenioid-theoretic formulation is technically ill-suited to conjugate synchronization. (ii) Such complications do not occur for realifications (R_{>=0}(double-dagger D^vdash)_v, D^{vdash-vdash}(double-dagger D^vdash) of Corollary 4.5 (ii)). Frobenioid-theoretic formulations are typically easier than monoid-theoretic ones when the Picard groups Pic_Phi(-) ([FrdI] Theorems 5.1, 6.4 (i); [IUTchI] Remark 3.1.5) contain nontorsion elements, i.e. when there is a nontrivial degree of line bundles; examples are global arithmetic Frobenioids such as D^{vdash-vdash}(double-dagger D^vdash) of Corollary 4.5 (ii) and the tempered Frobenioids of Propositions 3.3, 3.4 and Corollary 3.6.
IUT2.Rem4_5_1.conclusion: The monoids of Corollary 4.5 (i), (iv) give F-prime-strips and F^vdash-prime-strips, the latter for the theta and Gaussian monoids only up to an indeterminacy at bad v by automorphisms of the split Frobenioid that are the identity on isometries; realifications avoid this, and Frobenioid formulations suit settings with a nontrivial degree.

IUT2.Rem4_5_3.content: Significance of the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry giving the symmetrizing isomorphisms of Corollary 4.5 (iii) (Remark 3.5.2). (i) Conjugate synchronization (Corollaries 3.5 (i), 4.5 (iii); Propositions 4.1 (iii), 4.3 (iii)) is possible for the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry but not for the F_l^*-symmetry precisely because of the connectedness, at each v, of the local components involved (Remarks 2.6.1 (i), 2.6.2 (i), 3.5.2 (ii); [IUTchI] Remark 6.12.4 (i), (ii)); similar, easier remarks hold at good v. A related property, not shared by F_l^*, is the geometric nature of the automorphisms giving the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry (Remark 3.5.2 (iii)). (ii) Comparison of the single-basepoint symmetrizing isomorphisms with multi-basepoint symmetries (Remarks 3.5.3, 4.5.2 (ii)): (a) unlike mono-analytic capsules/processions, the ring structure (arithmetic holomorphic structure) stays intact, which is essential for the log-wall (Remark 3.6.4 (i); [IUTchIII]); (b) unlike holomorphic capsules/processions, the single basepoint gives conjugate synchronization and a bijective link with the labels LabCusp^{+-}(-) (Remark 3.5.2), both crucial for Galois-theoretic theta evaluation (Corollaries 3.5, 3.6; Remark 3.8.3); (c) the F_l^{x+-}-symmetries of D-Theta^ell-bridges keep a bijective link with LabCusp^{+-}(-) ([IUTchI] Remarks 4.9.2 (i), 6.12.4 (i)) but, being multi-basepoint, do not give conjugate synchronization. (iii) Gluing the local F_l^{x+-}-symmetries of Corollary 3.5 (i) and Propositions 4.1 (iii), 4.3 (iii) into the global F_l^{x+-}-symmetry of Corollary 4.5 (iii) requires the global portion dagger D^{circledcirc +-} of the D-Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theater ([IUTchI] Proposition 6.5, Remark 6.12.4 (iii)), which synchronizes the +- indeterminacies at each v; this is the content of [IUTchI] Proposition 6.5, and these local +- indeterminacies are an important cause of the profinite conjugacy (Delta-hat-conjugacy) indeterminacies of Corollaries 2.4, 2.5 (Remark 2.5.2), hence of the need for the complements on tempered coverings of [IUTchI] Section 2 in the proof of Corollary 2.4.

IUT2.Rem4_5_3.conclusion: Conjugate synchronization holds for the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry (single basepoint, connected local components, geometric automorphisms) and not for the F_l^*-symmetry; it keeps the ring structure and the bijective link with labels; the global F_l^{x+-}-symmetry needs the global portion dagger D^{circledcirc +-} to synchronize the local +- indeterminacies.

The comparisons in (ii) are commentary.

IUT2.Rem4_7_2.content: In the context of Corollary 4.7 (ii): unlike the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry, the F_l^*-symmetry does not allow the conjugate synchronization of Corollary 4.5 (iii), since it arises from conjugation by elements with nontrivial image in the arithmetic portion (the absolute Galois group of the base field) of the global arithmetic fundamental groups (Remarks 3.5.2 (iii), 4.5.3 (i); Remark 2.5.2 (iii) on G_K-conjugacy indeterminacies giving G_v-conjugacy indeterminacies). This forces Corollary 4.7 (ii) to work with (a) F-prime-strips rather than ind-topological monoids with Galois actions, and (b) objects of Corollary 4.7 (i) with sub- or superscripts mod, sol, kappa-sol, infinity-kappa (F_mod, F_sol, pi_1^{kappa-sol}(-), infinity-kappa-coric rational functions), or (as for pi_1^{rat/kappa-sol}(-)) objects defined only up to certain conjugacy indeterminacies. Both let one ignore the independent, non-synchronizable conjugacy indeterminacies at distinct labels arising from the single basepoint (Remark 3.5.2 (ii)). With the objects marked mod, sol or kappa-sol, on which the conjugacy indeterminacies act in a synchronized way, the diagonal subcategories of the Frobenioids can be built without the subtleties of independent indeterminacies at distinct labels (Remark 3.8.3 (ii)). In [IUTchIII] the ring structure on the objects with subscript mod serves as a translation apparatus between boxplus-line bundles (additive) and boxtimes-line bundles (multiplicative, as in Frobenioids) ([AbsTopIII] Definition 5.3 (i), (ii)).
IUT2.Rem4_7_2.conclusion: Conjugate synchronization is impossible for the F_l^*-symmetry, because it arises from conjugation by elements with nontrivial image in the absolute Galois group of the base field; therefore Corollary 4.7 (ii) works with F-prime-strips and with objects (mod, sol, kappa-sol, infinity-kappa) on which conjugacy indeterminacies are synchronized or which are defined only up to conjugacy.
definitions_required: F_mod, F_sol, pi_1^{kappa-sol}, infinity-kappa-coric rational functions ([IUTchI] Examples 5.1, 5.4)
obligations: Page 143: the impossibility of conjugate synchronization for the F_l^*-symmetry is recalled from Remarks 3.5.2 (iii) and 4.5.3 (i) and is not proved; no precise statement of 'impossible' is given.

IUT2.Rem4_7_4.content: Combinatorial models of the uniradiality of the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry and the multiradiality of the F_l^*-symmetry (Remark 4.7.3 (ii), (iii)). (i) Relative to an arithmetic holomorphic structure (a Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater, [IUTchI] Definition 6.13 (i)), the etale-picture of each symmetry ([IUTchI] Corollaries 4.12, 6.10) is a collection of copies of F_l (respectively |F_l| = F_l^* union {0}), one per arithmetic holomorphic structure (spoke alpha), glued at the coric label 0, each with an action of a copy of F_l^{x+-} (respectively F_l^*) (Figs. 4.1, 4.2). (ii) (a) For F_l^{x+-} the actions on distinct spokes fail to commute; (b) for F_l^* they commute and are compatible with the permutations of spokes ([IUTchI] Corollary 4.12 (iii)). The noncommutativity (incompatibility with simultaneous execution at distinct spokes, Remark 1.9.1) is a direct consequence of including the zero label in the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry, a prototypical combinatorial representation of uniradiality; the commutativity follows from excluding the zero label from F_l^*, a prototype of multiradiality; and for F_l^{x+-}, invariance under the actions on all spokes is a kind of uniformity, hence coricity (Remark 4.7.3 (ii)). (iii) A formulation as radial environments (Example 1.7 (ii)): coric data are objects 0_alpha, with exactly one arrow (alpha, beta) from 0_alpha to 0_beta; radial data are copies (F_l)_alpha (respectively |F_l|_alpha), and the set of arrows (F_l)_alpha -> (F_l)_beta (respectively |F_l|_alpha -> |F_l|_beta) has exactly one element if the actions of (F_l^{x+-})_gamma on (F_l)_gamma (respectively (F_l^*)_gamma on |F_l|_gamma), gamma = alpha, beta, determine an action of (F_l^{x+-})_alpha x (F_l^{x+-})_beta (respectively (F_l^*)_alpha x (F_l^*)_beta) on the coproduct (F_l)_alpha coprod_0 (F_l)_beta (respectively for |F_l|) obtained by identifying 0_alpha and 0_beta, and is empty otherwise; the radial functor sends (F_l)_alpha to 0_alpha (respectively |F_l|_alpha to 0_alpha). The resulting radial environment is said to be easily seen to be uniradial (respectively multiradial); details left to the reader. The product formulation recalls the switching functor of Example 1.7 (iii) and parallel transport (Remark 1.7.1).
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Remark 4.7.3; F_l^{x+-} acting on F_l and F_l^* acting on |F_l| as in [IUTchI] (not redefined on these pages)
IUT2.Rem4_7_4.conclusion: (ii) The F_l^{x+-}-actions on distinct spokes of the etale-picture fail to commute (uniradiality), while the F_l^*-actions commute and are compatible with permutations of spokes (multiradiality); (iii) the combinatorial radial environment built from these actions is uniradial for F_l^{x+-} and multiradial for F_l^*.

This is a finite combinatorial statement (about actions of the finite groups F_l^{x+-} and F_l^* of [IUTchI] on F_l and |F_l|) and a candidate for a Lean formalization with Mathlib's ZMod and category theory, once the convention for identity arrows (see ambiguities) is fixed.

IUT2.Rem4_7_5.content: The F_l^{x+-}- and F_l^*-symmetries correspond to the additive and multiplicative structures of F_l, a finite approximation of Z (Remark 4.7.3 (i)): (a) to the two combinatorial dimensions, addition and multiplication, of a ring ([AbsTopIII] Section I3); (b) to the units and value group of a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean or complex archimedean local field; or (c) to the two cohomological dimensions of the absolute Galois group of a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field, or the two real dimensions of a complex archimedean field. The hierarchy of these dimensions (multiplication piled on addition) is reflected in (d) the subordination structure (nonzero labels <<< zero label) for weighted volumes (Remark 4.7.3 (iii)), and (e) in the fact that the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry arises from conjugation by the geometric fundamental group (Remarks 3.5.2 (iii), 4.5.3 (i)) and the F_l^*-symmetry from conjugation by the absolute Galois group of the global base field (Remark 4.7.2), the arithmetic fundamental groups having a hierarchical extension structure.
IUT2.Rem4_7_5.conclusion: The two symmetries are interpreted as the additive and multiplicative dimensions of a ring, with corresponding interpretations (units and value group; cohomological or real dimensions), and their hierarchy appears in the subordination of nonzero to zero labels and in the geometric versus arithmetic origin of the symmetries.
obligations: Interpretive commentary; the statement in (e) about the origin of the symmetries is recalled from the cited remarks.

IUT2.Rem4_7_6.content: In the context of Corollary 4.7 (i), non-realified global Frobenioids (corresponding to F_mod) make sense only for the F_l^*-symmetry. To treat F_mod anabelianly one needs the full profinite group Pi_{C_F}, not only its open subgroups Pi_{C_K}, Pi_{X_K} (underlined) giving the global portions of the F_l^*- and F_l^{x+-}-symmetries ([IUTchI] Definitions 4.1 (v), 6.1 (v)); for the abstract topological group Pi_{C_F} these subgroups are well defined only up to Pi_{C_F}-conjugacy, i.e. up to automorphisms from their normalizers in Pi_{C_F} ([IUTchI] Remark 6.12.6 (iii), (iv)), so they are subject to indeterminacies from the natural F_l^*-poly-actions ([IUTchI] Example 4.3 (iv)), i.e. the natural F_l^*-symmetries. One cannot form the quotient by this indeterminacy, since this would give label-crushing, identifying the distinct labels j in F_l^* that are crucial for the Gaussian monoids ([IUTchI] Remark 4.7.1). Then the F_l^*-symmetries of Pi_{C_K}, Pi_{X_K} necessarily involve conjugation by elements of the absolute Galois groups of the global base fields, hence are fundamentally incompatible with conjugate synchronization (Remark 4.7.2). So one must (a) isolate the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry from the F_l^*-symmetry to establish conjugate synchronization and (b) isolate the F_l^*-symmetry from the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry to work with Galois-theoretic representations of the global base field F_mod: the dismantling of the two a priori intertwined combinatorial dimensions of a ring (Remarks 4.7.3, 4.7.5; [AbsTopIII] Section I3).
IUT2.Rem4_7_6.conclusion: Non-realified global Frobenioids such as F_mod are available only with the F_l^*-symmetry; working with the abstract group Pi_{C_F} subjects Pi_{C_K}, Pi_{X_K} to F_l^*-indeterminacies that cannot be quotiented out without label-crushing and are incompatible with conjugate synchronization, so the two symmetries must be isolated from each other.
obligations: Page 148: the claim that non-realified global Frobenioids make sense only for the F_l^*-symmetry is supported by the discussion of Pi_{C_F}-conjugacy but not proved; the incompatibility with conjugate synchronization (page 149) rests on Remark 4.7.2.

IUT2.Rem4_8_1.content: (i) The Frobenioid C^{vdash-vdash}_gau(dagger HT^Theta) of Corollary 4.6 (v), constructed as a subcategory of a product over j in F_l^* of copies dagger C^{vdash-vdash}_j of dagger C^{vdash-vdash}, may, via the isomorphism dagger C^{vdash-vdash}_j -> (dagger F^{circledast R}_mod)_j of Corollary 4.8 (iii), be regarded as a subcategory of the product over j in F_l^* of (dagger F^{circledast R}_mod)_j. (ii) The local data at v in V of Psi_{F_gau}(dagger HT^Theta) (Corollary 4.6 (iv)) give split Frobenioids F_gau(dagger HT^Theta)_v (Definition 3.8 (ii) at bad v), an F^vdash-prime-strip F_gau(dagger HT^Theta), and its realification F_gau(dagger HT^Theta)^R; by the construction of Corollary 4.6 (iv), the realified Frobenioid of F_gau(dagger HT^Theta)^R at each v is naturally poly-embedded in the product over j in F_l^* of (dagger F_>^R)_j, and, by the full poly-isomorphisms (dagger F_>)_j -> dagger F_j (tautologically compatible with the labels j), in the product over j in F_l^* of dagger F_j^R. (iii) Via these poly-embeddings, the realified localization functors (dagger F^{circledast R}_mod)_j -> dagger F_j^R of Corollary 4.8 (iii) induce a realified localization functor (up to isomorphism) C^{vdash-vdash}_gau(dagger HT^Theta) -> F_gau(dagger HT^Theta)^R, which, as one verifies immediately, is compatible (compare Corollary 4.8 (iii)) with the realified localization isomorphisms Phi_{C^{vdash-vdash}_gau(dagger HT^Theta), v} -> Psi_{F_gau}(dagger HT^Theta)^R_v of Corollary 4.6 (v), for v in V.
IUT2.Rem4_8_1.conclusion: C^{vdash-vdash}_gau(dagger HT^Theta) embeds in the product over j of (dagger F^{circledast R}_mod)_j; F_gau(dagger HT^Theta)^R poly-embeds in the product over j of dagger F_j^R; the realified localization functors of Corollary 4.8 (iii) induce a realified localization functor C^{vdash-vdash}_gau(dagger HT^Theta) -> F_gau(dagger HT^Theta)^R compatible with the localization isomorphisms of Corollary 4.6 (v).
