IUT2.Rem4_11_2.content: Summary of the theory so far, in four parts. (i) A Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater ([IUTchI] Definition 6.13 (i)) is a model of conventional scheme-theoretic arithmetic geometry around the theta function at primes of bad reduction in V^bad of the elliptic curve; it is a bridge between the number field and theta functions, realized by the Gaussian distribution, a globalized version of the theta values {q_v^{j^2}}, 1 <= j <= l^*, at l-torsion points (Remark 3.6.2 (iii); the value at label j is the mu_{2l}-orbit of q_v^{j^2} with q_v the chosen 2l-th root of the Tate parameter, Remark 2.5.1 (i)); 'Gaussian distribution' informally includes Gaussian monoids and Gaussian Frobenioids; it allows the non-scheme/ring-theoretic Theta^{x mu}_gau-link between distinct Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theaters (Corollary 4.10 (iii)). (ii) Within one Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater, the theta functions of [EtTh] give a single connected geometric Kummer theory-compatible theater for evaluating the theta function; its etale realization has a multiradial formulation (Section 1, Corollary 1.12), and its connectedness gives conjugate synchronization between the copies of the absolute Galois group of the base field at the evaluation points (Remark 2.6.1), compatible with the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry (Remark 3.5.2; Corollaries 4.5 (iii), 4.6 (iii)) of the D-Theta^ell-bridge ([IUTchI] Proposition 6.8 (i)); conjugate synchronization is essential for the coricity of the units (Corollary 4.10 (iv)) compatibly with the anabelian (etale) and post-anabelian (Frobenioid) representations of the Gaussian monoids (Remark 3.8.3); the post-anabelian representation is needed for the Theta^{x mu}_gau-link (Remarks 3.6.2 (ii), 3.8.3 (i)), the anabelian one for the log-wall in [IUTchIII] (Remark 3.8.3 (ii)); the canonical splittings into unit and value group components at bad v correspond to the non-deformed and Teichmuller-dilated real dimensions of complex Teichmuller theory (Remark 4.10.3 (i), (ii)) and are crucial for log-shells. (iii) The number fields of the underlying ThetaNF-Hodge theater ([IUTchI] Section 5) will relate, via their ring structure, boxtimes-line bundles to boxplus-line bundles (Remark 4.7.2), which needs all primes ([AbsTopIII] Remark 5.10.2 (iv)); such constructions are compatible with the F_l^*-symmetry ([IUTchI] Proposition 4.9 (i)), which is combinatorially multiradial and associated with value groups, while the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry is combinatorially uniradial and associated with units (Remarks 4.7.3 to 4.7.5); the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry is compatible with conjugate synchronization, which can only be established after isolating the prime-strips from the conjugacy indeterminacies inherent in the global absolute Galois group (Remark 4.7.2), i.e. free of the combinatorial constraints of the prime-trees ([IUTchI] Remark 4.3.1). Both symmetries share connectedness of the global objects of their Theta^ell- and NF-bridges, essential for bookkeeping of the labels of evaluation points (Remarks 3.5.2, 4.5.3 (iii); [IUTchI] Remark 4.9.2 (i)), which cannot be done with formal products of local objects instead of a global number field ([AbsTopIII] Remark 3.7.6 (v)); with the profinite global geometric fundamental groups this requires the complements on tempered coverings of [IUTchI] Section 2 (Remark 4.5.3 (iii)). (iv) The Gaussian-distribution bridge is built by dismantling the characteristic topography obstructing the relation of theta functions to number fields: for theta functions, the geometric dimension of the tempered coverings at bad v, resolved by evaluation at l-torsion points (a rough finite approximation, [HASurI] Section 1.3.4); for number fields, the prime-trees that give conjugacy indeterminacies obstructing conjugate synchronization, resolved by working with prime-strips labeled by F_l^* ([IUTchI] Remark 4.3.1); combinatorially this is dismantling the ring F_l, a rough finite approximation of Z ([IUTchI] Remark 6.12.3 (i)), into its additive and multiplicative parts, the F_l^{x+-}- and F_l^*-symmetries.
implicit_hypotheses: The setting of Sections 1 to 4 and of [IUTchI]
IUT2.Rem4_11_2.conclusion: A Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater bridges number fields and theta functions through the Gaussian distribution of theta values q_v^{j^2} at l-torsion points; conjugate synchronization (from connectedness and the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry) gives coricity of units; the F_l^*-symmetry is compatible with the global ring structure; the bridge is built by dismantling the geometric dimension (via evaluation) and the prime-trees (via labeled prime-strips), i.e. the additive and multiplicative parts of F_l.
definitions_required: Gaussian distribution, Gaussian monoids, Gaussian Frobenioids
obligations: Summary commentary; the assertions it summarizes are those of the cited corollaries and remarks, whose records carry the corresponding statuses.
ambiguities: Page 166: 'distibutions' is a misprint for 'distributions'.

Page 165: the theta values are displayed as {q_v^{j^2}}, 1 <= j <= l^*, with q_v doubly underlined; per Remark 2.5.1 (i) (page 72) q_v is the chosen 2l-th root of the Tate parameter and each value is determined up to mu_{2l}.

IUT2.Rem4_11_3.content: In the context of Remark 4.11.2: from the combinatorics of the F_l^{x+-}- and F_l^*-symmetries one has the correspondences Theta^ell <-> boxplus and NF <-> boxtimes (the Theta^ell-bridge corresponds to the additive F_l^{x+-}-symmetry, the NF-bridge to the multiplicative F_l^*-symmetry), whereas at the level of line bundles one has Theta^ell <-> boxtimes and NF <-> boxplus: arithmetic line bundles are treated multiplicatively, via monoids or Frobenioids, in the Theta^ell-bridge, while the equivalence of boxtimes- and boxplus-line bundles is realized only via the global ring structure of the number fields of the NF-bridge ([IUTchI] Section 5). This juggling of boxplus and boxtimes is a combinatorial counterpart of the juggling of boxplus and boxtimes in the theory of the log-wall ([AbsTopIII] Section I3).
IUT2.Rem4_11_3.conclusion: The combinatorial correspondences (Theta^ell with addition, NF with multiplication) are reversed at the level of line bundles (Theta^ell with multiplicative, boxtimes, line bundles; NF with boxplus via the global ring structure); this is a combinatorial counterpart of the log-wall.
obligations: Page 168: that boxtimes- and boxplus-line bundles can be related only through the global ring structure ('may only be realized') is stated without proof; the rest is interpretive commentary.

IUT2.Rem4_11_4.content: Analogies between the theory and scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory and p-adic Teichmuller theory, in three parts: (i) theta values at l-torsion points as deformations of the holomorphic structure; (ii) the chains of Theta^{x mu}- and Theta^{x mu}_gau-links as canonical liftings and the passage from MF^nabla-objects to Galois representations; (iii) correspondences (a) to (d) with [CanLift] Section 3.
obligations: Parent of the part records; the status of each part is given there.

IUT2.Rem4_11_4.i.content: (i) In scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory the l-torsion points of an elliptic curve are a rough finite approximation of the two real dimensions of the underlying one-dimensional complex torus ([HASurI] Section 1.3.4), corresponding to a holomorphic dimension and a one-dimensional deformation of it ([HASurI] Section 1.4.2). The present theory works with an elliptic curve isogenous to the given one by an isogeny of degree l (X underlined rather than X), so the holomorphic dimension can be neglected and one concentrates on its deformations ([EtTh] Introduction): the possible values at the l-torsion evaluation points are possible deformations of the holomorphic structure and the specific theta values a specific deformation. The parameter 0 != t in LabCusp^{+-}(-) indexing these values, linear in the group structure like the tangent space of the elliptic curve, descends (especially for the ThetaNF-Hodge theater) to j in F_l^*, a kind of square (F_l^x)^2 of F_l^x, hence quadratic like the square of the tangent space, naturally isomorphic to the tangent space of the moduli space of elliptic curves at the given curve. As in Remark 3.6.2 (iii), in the context of the Theta^{x mu}_gau-link the theta values are a deformation between the identity and a Frobenius morphism, and the theta function a continuous version of it.
IUT2.Rem4_11_4.i.conclusion: Theta values at l-torsion points are interpreted as a specific deformation of the holomorphic structure; the label j in F_l^* is quadratic in t, like the square of the tangent space, i.e. the tangent space of the moduli of elliptic curves.
obligations: Interpretive analogy. The arithmetic fact behind 'quadratic' (the label j corresponds to t^2, i.e. F_l^* viewed as a square of F_l^x) is consistent with the theta values q^{j^2} of Remark 2.5.1 (i) (page 72) but is not stated as a theorem here.
ambiguities: Page 168: 'linear which respect to' is a misprint for 'linear with respect to'.

Page 168: j in F_l^* is called a 'square (F_l^x)^2' of F_l^x; F_l^* is F_l^x/{+-1}, which is isomorphic to the group of squares (F_l^x)^2 via squaring, a reading the page indicates only by 'may be thought of as'.

IUT2.Rem4_11_4.ii.content: (ii) In the analogy with p-adic Teichmuller theory ([AbsTopIII] Section I5), the infinite chain ... -> ^{(n-1)}HT^{Theta^{+-ell}NF} -> ^{n}HT^{Theta^{+-ell}NF} -> ... -> ^{0}HT^{Theta^{+-ell}NF} of Theta^{x mu}-links of Corollary 4.10 (vi), parametrized by n <= 0, corresponds to the canonical liftings: each Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater (the conventional scheme theory around a given number field with an elliptic curve) corresponds to a hyperbolic curve in positive characteristic with a nilpotent ordinary indigenous bundle; the theta functions giving the Theta^{x mu}-links specify the canonical deformation; the canonical Frobenius lifting corresponds to the theory of [IUTchIII]. The passage from theta functions and number fields to Gaussian distributions (Remark 4.11.2), via Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation from that chain to the corresponding chain of Theta^{x mu}_gau-links, corresponds to the passage from MF^nabla-objects to Galois representations for canonical indigenous bundles ([pTeich] Introduction, Sections 1.3, 1.7; [HASurI] Sections 1.3, 1.4): from a curve with a canonical Frobenius-invariant indigenous bundle to a curve with a canonical crystalline Galois representation of the arithmetic fundamental group of the generic fiber into PGL_2(Z_p).
IUT2.Rem4_11_4.ii.conclusion: The chain of Theta^{x mu}-links corresponds to canonical liftings, and the passage to the chain of Theta^{x mu}_gau-links via Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation corresponds to the passage from MF^nabla-objects to Galois representations in p-adic Teichmuller theory.
obligations: Analogy only; no mathematical claim to formalize.

IUT2.Rem4_11_4.iii.content: (iii) Technical correspondences with [CanLift] Section 3 (see also Remark 4.11.5): (a) the discussion of (ii) recalls the role of the canonical Galois representation in the absolute p-adic anabelian theory of [CanLift] Section 3 (proof of [CanLift] Lemma 3.5); (b) mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity (Definition 1.1 (ii), Remark 1.1.1) recalls the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms of [CanLift] Section 3 via [AbsAnab] Section 2 (Lemmas 2.5, 2.6) (Remark 1.11.6), but at the level of direct correspondence is better compared with the local uniformizations from the canonical indigenous bundle (Remark 3.6.5 (iii)); (c) the two-dimensional symmetry formed by the F_l^{x+-}- and F_l^*-symmetries (two real dimensions of the complex upper half-plane, [IUTchI] Remark 6.12.3 (iii)) recalls the vanishing of H^0(Ad(-)) of the canonical Galois representation ([CanLift] Lemma 3.2): the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry corresponds to unipotent monodromy over the ordinary locus, the matrices (1 *; 0 1), isomorphic to the additive group F_p; the F_l^*-symmetry to toral monodromy at the supersingular points, the matrices (* 0; 0 *^{-1}), isomorphic to F_p^x, arising from extracting a (p-1)-th root of the Hasse invariant; the conventional theory on one connected component of the ordinary locus (with q-parameters) recalls the uniradial F_l^{x+-}-symmetry, and supersingular points lying simultaneously on closures of distinct components recalls the multiradial F_l^*-symmetry (Remark 4.7.4); summarized in Fig. 4.4 (additive/multiplicative, uniradial/multiradial, monodromy over the ordinary locus/at the supersingular points); (d) conjugate synchronization at the evaluation points, giving the Gaussian distribution and the links between the Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theaters of the second chain of (ii), recalls [CanLift] Lemma 3.4, describing H^1(Ad(-)) of the canonical Galois representation, whose slope -1 portion governs the links between mod p^n and mod p^{n+1} (proof of [CanLift] Lemma 3.5) and is, up to tensor with an unramified representation, a direct product of 3g-3+r copies of F_p(-1) (Tate twist), recalling the l^* synchronized copies of cyclotomes in the evaluation of the theta function; deformations of the canonical Galois representation parametrized by H^1(Ad(-)) correspond to the independent Aut(G_v)-indeterminacies (v in V^non) at each label in F_l^* for multiradial representations of Gaussian monoids ([IUTchIII] Section 3, Remark 3.12.4 (iii)). The page notes that the '-1's in (d) should be replaced by '1's (Remark 4.11.5). The description in [CanLift] Lemma 3.4 reflects ordinarity (not just admissibility) of the indigenous bundle, recalling [AbsTopIII] Remark 5.10.3 (ii) on ordinarity and the etale theta function.
IUT2.Rem4_11_4.iii.conclusion: Correspondences (a) to (d) with [CanLift] Section 3, including Fig. 4.4: F_l^{x+-}-symmetry with additive, uniradial, unipotent monodromy over the ordinary locus; F_l^*-symmetry with multiplicative, multiradial, toral monodromy at supersingular points.
definitions_required: canonical Galois representation; H^0(Ad(-)), H^1(Ad(-)) ([CanLift] Section 3)
obligations: Analogies only; the cited facts about [CanLift] are external. The statement that the slope -1 portion is a direct product of 3g-3+r copies of F_p(-1) is quoted from [CanLift] Lemma 3.4 and corrected (sign of the Tate twist) by Remark 4.11.5.
ambiguities: Page 171: the paper itself says that the '-1's in (d) should be '1's (Remark 4.11.5), i.e. the 'slope -1 portion' and F_p(-1) are affected by the sign error in [CanLift] Lemma 3.4; the record keeps the text as printed and notes the correction.

IUT2.Rem4_11_5.content: Corrections to the statement of condition (dagger_M) of [CanLift] Lemma 3.4, said not to affect its proof substantively: the subquotient G^2(M) (respectively G^{-1}) should be G^{-2}(M) (respectively G^1); G^{-2}(M) (respectively G^1) is isomorphic to the tensor product of an unramified module with the Tate twist F_p(-2) (respectively F_p(1)), so the Tate twists in (dagger_M) have a sign error; and, to get the desired dimensions over F_p, the module M := H^1(Delta_{X^log}, Ad(V_{F_p})) must be replaced by its submodule of elements whose restriction to each cuspidal inertia group of Delta_{X^log} is upper triangular for the filtration given by the nilpotent monodromy on V_{F_p}; an elementary computation shows that this restriction lowers the dimension of G^{-2}(M) from 3g-3+2r to 3g-3+r.
explicit_hypotheses: The setting of [CanLift] Lemma 3.4: M := H^1(Delta_{X^log}, Ad(V_{F_p})) with its filtration G^*
IUT2.Rem4_11_5.conclusion: In [CanLift] Lemma 3.4: G^2(M), G^{-1} should read G^{-2}(M), G^1, with Tate twists F_p(-2), F_p(1); and M must be replaced by the submodule of classes upper triangular at each cuspidal inertia group, which lowers dim G^{-2}(M) from 3g-3+2r to 3g-3+r.
obligations: Page 172: the dimension drop from 3g-3+2r to 3g-3+r is attributed to 'an elementary computation' that is not written out; the claim that the corrections do not affect the proof of [CanLift] Lemma 3.4 in any substantive way is asserted without argument. A check would need [CanLift] Lemma 3.4 and its proof (external).
ambiguities: The index gives pages 172 to 173; page 173 is the bibliography, so the remark ends on page 172.
Page 172: g and r (presumably the genus and number of cusps of the curve of [CanLift]) are not defined on this page.
